at bade.explanation: "At bade" means "to bathe" and also "to swim", going into the sea or a lake for fun or to cool off. It is not for racing or training laps.

sentence.da: Vi vil gerne **bade** i havet i dag.
sentence.en: We would like to swim in the sea today.

at bagatellisere.explanation: "At bagatellisere" means "to downplay", to make a problem sound smaller than it is. It comes from en bagatel (a trifle), something of little importance.

sentence.da: Politikerne vil **bagatellisere** problemet, men det er alvorligt.
sentence.en: The politicians want to downplay the problem, but it is serious.

at bage.explanation: "At bage" means "to bake", for things like cakes and bread. Do not mix it up with at stege (to fry), which is what you do with meat or eggs in a pan.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **bage** en kage i ovnen.
sentence.en: I want to bake a cake in the oven.

at bakke op.explanation: "At bakke op" means "to back up" or "to support" a person or a decision, usually followed by om: Vi bakker op om hendes forslag (We back up her proposal). It is not used for copying computer files, which is at sikkerhedskopiere (to back up files).

sentence.da: Hele klassen vil **bakke op** om læreren.
sentence.en: The whole class will back up the teacher.

at balancere.explanation: "At balancere" means "to balance": to keep yourself or something steady, for example on a rope or a narrow wall. It is also used for finding the right mix between two things: Hun balancerer arbejde og familie (She balances work and family).

sentence.da: Børnene kan **balancere** på en smal bom.
sentence.en: The children can balance on a narrow beam.

at bande.explanation: "At bande" means "to swear (curse)", saying rude words when you are angry. To swear a promise, use at sværge (to swear): Jeg sværger (I swear).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **bande** foran børnene.
sentence.en: You must not swear in front of the children.

at banke på.explanation: "At banke på" means "to knock", for example on a door. Without på, at banke means to beat: Hjertet banker (The heart beats).

sentence.da: Du skal **banke på**, når døren er lukket.
sentence.en: You have to knock when the door is closed.

at barbere.explanation: "At barbere" means "to shave", and you add sig when you shave yourself: Han barberer sig hver morgen (He shaves every morning). Without sig, you shave someone or something else: Lægen barberer området før operationen (The doctor shaves the area before the surgery).

sentence.da: Med en barbermaskine kan man **barbere** sit skæg af på få minutter.
sentence.en: With an electric shaver you can shave off your beard in a few minutes.

at barbere sig.explanation: "At barbere sig" means "to shave", taking the hair off your face or body with a razor. Sig shows that you do it to yourself. To shave someone else, leave it out: Jeg barberer ham (I shave him).

sentence.da: Han har skæg og vil **barbere sig**.
sentence.en: He has a beard and wants to shave.

at bearbejde.explanation: "At bearbejde" means "to process" or "to work on": to put work into a material or a text until it is in better shape, such as wood, metal or a draft. It is also used for coming to terms with something hard: Hun bearbejder sin sorg (She is processing her grief).

sentence.da: Snedkeren skal **bearbejde** træet og bygge et skab.
sentence.en: The carpenter must work the wood and build a cabinet.

at bebo.explanation: "At bebo" means "to inhabit", to live in a place. Unlike at bo i (to live in), it takes the place directly: Familien bebor huset (The family inhabits the house).

sentence.da: Kun få kan **bebo** den lille ø om vinteren.
sentence.en: Only a few can inhabit the small island in winter.

at bebrejde.explanation: "At bebrejde" means "to blame", to tell someone it is their fault. The pattern is at bebrejde nogen noget (to blame someone for something): Jeg bebrejder mig selv (I blame myself).

sentence.da: Du kan ikke **bebrejde** ham, at han var bange.
sentence.en: You cannot blame him for being scared.

at bede.explanation: "At bede" means "to ask" when you want something done or given. It also means "to pray": Hun beder til Gud (She prays to God). To ask a question, use at spørge (to ask a question).

sentence.da: Må jeg **bede** dig om hjælp?
sentence.en: May I ask you for help?

at bede om.explanation: "At bede om" means "to ask for" something you would like to get. Om comes before the thing you want. To ask a question, use at spørge (to ask).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **bede om** en kop kaffe.
sentence.en: I would like to ask for a cup of coffee.

at bedrage.explanation: "At bedrage" means "to deceive", to trick someone so that they believe something false. About a partner it also means "to cheat on": Han bedrog hende (He cheated on her).

sentence.da: Man må ikke **bedrage** kunderne med falske tilbud.
sentence.en: You must not deceive the customers with false offers.

at bedømme.explanation: "At bedømme" means "to judge" or "to assess": to decide how good something is, such as a contest entry, an exam or a risk. In court the verb is at dømme (to sentence): Retten dømmer manden til fængsel (The court sentences the man to prison).

sentence.da: Dommerne skal **bedømme** kagerne i konkurrencen.
sentence.en: The judges must judge the cakes in the contest.

at befinde sig.explanation: "At befinde sig" means "to be located": to be in a certain place or situation. In everyday talk Danes just say at være (to be): Hvor er du? (Where are you?)

sentence.da: Hotellet skal **befinde sig** tæt på stranden, fordi vi vil bade.
sentence.en: The hotel has to be near the beach, because we want to swim.

at befri.explanation: "At befri" means "to free" or "to liberate": to let someone out of prison, danger or a heavy burden. Pengene befrier ham for bekymringer (The money frees him from worries).

sentence.da: Soldaterne vil **befri** fangerne fra fængslet.
sentence.en: The soldiers will free the prisoners from the prison.

at begejstre.explanation: "At begejstre" means "to thrill" or "to excite": to make someone happy and enthusiastic about something. It is not for nervous excitement, which is spændt (excited, eager): Jeg er spændt på resultatet (I am excited about the result).

sentence.da: Hendes tale kan **begejstre** hele salen.
sentence.en: Her speech can thrill the whole room.

at begrave.explanation: "At begrave" means "to bury": to put something in the ground, most often a dead person or a pet. It can also mean dropping an idea for good: De begravede planen (They buried the plan).

sentence.da: Piraterne vil **begrave** skatten på en øde ø.
sentence.en: The pirates will bury the treasure on a deserted island.

at begrunde.explanation: "At begrunde" means "to justify": to say why you decided or think something. It is common at school and at work, where you are asked to back up an answer: Kan du begrunde dit svar? (Can you justify your answer?)

sentence.da: Du skal **begrunde** din mening med gode eksempler.
sentence.en: You must justify your opinion with good examples.

at begrænse.explanation: "At begrænse" means "to limit": to keep an amount, a time or a size from growing past a point. With sig you limit yourself: Jeg begrænser mig til én kop kaffe (I limit myself to one cup of coffee).

sentence.da: Skolen vil **begrænse** brugen af mobiltelefoner i timerne.
sentence.en: The school wants to limit the use of cell phones in class.

at begunstige.explanation: "At begunstige" means "to favor", to give someone or something an advantage over others. It is often used for rules and systems: Loven begunstiger store firmaer (The law favors big companies).

sentence.da: Skatten vil **begunstige** familier med børn.
sentence.en: The tax will favor families with children.

at begynde.explanation: "At begynde" means "to begin" or "to start". You can use it with another action: Jeg begynder at læse (I begin to read). It also works alone: Skolen begynder i august (School begins in August).

sentence.da: Filmen skal **begynde** klokken otte.
sentence.en: The movie is going to begin at eight.

at begynde på.explanation: "At begynde på" means "to begin on" something new, like a task, a job or a course. It is close to at starte på (to start on).

sentence.da: Efter ferien skal jeg **begynde på** universitetet.
sentence.en: After the vacation, I am going to start at the university.

at begå.explanation: "At begå" means "to commit": to do something wrong or illegal. It goes with crimes and mistakes: begå en forbrydelse (commit a crime), begå en fejl (make a mistake). With sig it means something else: Hun kan begå sig på fransk (She can get by in French).

sentence.da: Tyven vil **begå** endnu et indbrud i nat.
sentence.en: The thief will commit another break-in tonight.

at behandle.explanation: "At behandle" means "to treat", both in medicine and in how you act toward people: Han behandler mig godt (He treats me well). It also means to handle a matter officially: Kommunen behandler sagen (The city is handling the case).

sentence.da: Lægen kan **behandle** sygdommen med medicin.
sentence.en: The doctor can treat the illness with medicine.

at beherske.explanation: "At beherske" means "to master" or "to control". For a skill you know well, such as a language, it means to have a good command of it: Hun behersker fransk (She has a good command of French). With sig (oneself) it means to stay in control of your feelings: Han kunne ikke beherske sig (He could not control himself).

sentence.da: Hun kan **beherske** tre sprog og taler dem flydende.
sentence.en: She has a good command of three languages and speaks them fluently.

at beholde.explanation: "At beholde" means "to keep" something you already have. For a promise, use at holde (to hold): Jeg holder mit løfte (I keep my promise).

sentence.da: Du må gerne **beholde** bogen.
sentence.en: You may keep the book.

at behøve.explanation: "At behøve" means "to need", and it is mostly used for needing to do something, with at (to): Du behøver ikke at komme (You do not need to come). For needing a thing, Danes usually say at have brug for: Jeg har brug for hjælp (I need help).

sentence.da: Du vil ikke **behøve** at betale.
sentence.en: You will not need to pay.

at bekende.explanation: "At bekende" means "to confess": to admit that you have done something wrong. With sig til it means to openly stand by a belief or an idea: Hun bekender sig til sine værdier (She stands by her values).

sentence.da: Hun vil **bekende**, at hun har taget pengene.
sentence.en: She will confess that she has taken the money.

at bekræfte.explanation: "At bekræfte" means "to confirm", saying that something is true or settled. It also works for showing that a guess was right: Testen bekræfter det (The test confirms it).

sentence.da: Kan du **bekræfte**, at mødet er klokken ti?
sentence.en: Can you confirm that the meeting is at ten o'clock?

at bekymre sig.explanation: "At bekymre sig" means "to worry", feeling uneasy about something that might go wrong. Add om for what you worry about: Jeg bekymrer mig om dig (I worry about you). The little word sig changes with the person: jeg bekymrer mig, du bekymrer dig.

sentence.da: Hun vil ikke **bekymre sig**, fordi alt går godt.
sentence.en: She won't worry because everything is going well.

at bekæmpe.explanation: "At bekæmpe" means "to fight" or "to combat": to work against something harmful, such as a disease, crime or poverty. It is not for a fistfight, which is at slås (to brawl).

sentence.da: Lægerne kan **bekæmpe** sygdommen med den nye medicin.
sentence.en: The doctors can fight the disease with the new medicine.

at belaste.explanation: "At belaste" means "to burden" or "to strain": to put heavy weight or pressure on something, such as a bridge, a knee or a budget. Kørsel belaster miljøet (Driving burdens the environment).

sentence.da: Tunge lastbiler kan **belaste** en gammel bro for meget.
sentence.en: Heavy trucks can strain an old bridge too much.

at belyse.explanation: "At belyse" means "to shed light on": to make a subject clearer by giving more facts. It also means to light something up: Projektøren belyser scenen (The spotlight lights up the stage).

sentence.da: Rapporten skal **belyse** problemet med flere tal.
sentence.en: The report must shed light on the problem with more figures.

at belære.explanation: "At belære" means "to lecture (someone)", to explain something to a person as if they know less than you. The tone is often annoying: Du skal ikke belære mig (Do not lecture me).

sentence.da: Han elsker at **belære** andre, men lytter sjældent selv.
sentence.en: He loves to lecture others but rarely listens himself.

at belønne.explanation: "At belønne" means "to reward": to give someone something nice because of good work or good behavior: Vi belønner hunden med en godbid (We reward the dog with a treat).

sentence.da: Chefen vil **belønne** de ansatte med en bonus.
sentence.en: The boss will reward the employees with a bonus.

at bemærke.explanation: "At bemærke" means "to notice" and also "to remark", meaning to say something in passing: Hun bemærkede, at det var koldt (She remarked that it was cold). Bemærk! at the start of a sentence means "Note!"

sentence.da: Du vil **bemærke** en stor forskel med det samme.
sentence.en: You will notice a big difference right away.

at benytte.explanation: "At benytte" means "to use", especially something that is available to you, such as a chance, a service or a road. With sig af it means to make use of something: Jeg benytter mig af tilbuddet (I am taking advantage of the offer).

sentence.da: Gæster kan **benytte** hotellets pool hele dagen.
sentence.en: Guests can use the hotel's pool all day.

at benægte.explanation: "At benægte" means "to deny": to say that something is not true: Han benægter, at han var der (He denies that he was there). To deny someone something, such as entry, is at nægte (to refuse).

sentence.da: Hun vil **benægte**, at hun har sagt det.
sentence.en: She will deny that she said it.

at beordre.explanation: "At beordre" means "to order (command)", to tell people what they must do when you have the authority, such as a boss or an officer: Chefen beordrede os hjem (The boss ordered us home). For food, use at bestille (to order).

sentence.da: Generalen kan **beordre** soldaterne til at blive.
sentence.en: The general can order the soldiers to stay.

at beregne.explanation: "At beregne" means "to calculate": to work out an amount with numbers, such as a price, a distance or a tax. Prisen beregnes ud fra vægten (The price is calculated from the weight).

sentence.da: Computeren kan **beregne** afstanden mellem byerne på et sekund.
sentence.en: The computer can calculate the distance between the cities in a second.

at berette.explanation: "At berette" means "to report" or "to tell", used for giving an account of what happened, often a longer one. It is often followed by om (about): Hun beretter om sin rejse (She tells about her trip).

sentence.da: Vidnet vil **berette** om ulykken i retten i morgen.
sentence.en: The witness will report on the accident in court tomorrow.

at berige.explanation: "At berige" means "to enrich", to make something fuller or more valuable. It is mostly used for life, culture and experiences: Rejser beriger livet (Travel enriches life). It can also be about money: Olien har beriget landet (The oil has enriched the country).

sentence.da: Nye venner kan **berige** dit liv mere end penge.
sentence.en: New friends can enrich your life more than money.

at berolige.explanation: "At berolige" means "to calm" or "to reassure": to make someone less afraid or upset, often with kind words. A medicine that does this is called et beroligende middel (a sedative).

sentence.da: Moren kan **berolige** barnet, når det græder.
sentence.en: The mother can calm the child when it cries.

at berøre.explanation: "At berøre" means "to touch" and "to affect": it is used for touching lightly, for moving someone emotionally and for matters that involve many people. Sagen berører mange (The matter affects many people). Jeg blev dybt berørt (I was deeply moved).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **berøre** maleriet på museet.
sentence.en: You must not touch the painting at the museum.

at besejre.explanation: "At besejre" means "to defeat": to win over an enemy, an opponent or a problem. It also fits fears and illnesses: Hun besejrede sin angst (She overcame her fear).

sentence.da: Holdet vil **besejre** de regerende mestre i finalen.
sentence.en: The team will defeat the reigning champions in the final.

at besidde.explanation: "At besidde" means "to possess", to have something valuable, or a quality such as knowledge or courage: Hun besidder stor viden (She possesses great knowledge). For everyday things, Danes just say at have (to have).

sentence.da: En god leder skal **besidde** mod og tålmodighed.
sentence.en: A good leader must possess courage and patience.

at beskadige.explanation: "At beskadige" means "to damage": to harm something so that it is broken or worse than before, such as a car, a wall or a book. The result is beskadiget (damaged): en beskadiget bil (a damaged car).

sentence.da: Stormen kan **beskadige** taget på det gamle hus.
sentence.en: The storm can damage the roof of the old house.

at beskatte.explanation: "At beskatte" means "to tax", to make people or goods pay money to the state: Staten beskatter alkohol hårdt (The state taxes alcohol heavily). It describes what the state does, not what you pay.

sentence.da: Regeringen vil **beskatte** de rigeste mere end i dag.
sentence.en: The government wants to tax the richest more than today.

at beskrive.explanation: "At beskrive" means "to describe". It is built from at skrive (to write), but it does not need paper: Kan du beskrive vejen til stationen? (Can you describe the way to the station?)

sentence.da: Kan du **beskrive** manden for politiet?
sentence.en: Can you describe the man for the police?

at beskylde.explanation: "At beskylde" means "to accuse", to say that someone has done something wrong. The charge comes after for: Han beskyldte hende for at lyve (He accused her of lying).

sentence.da: Du kan ikke **beskylde** ham for tyveri uden beviser.
sentence.en: You cannot accuse him of theft without proof.

at beskytte.explanation: "At beskytte" means "to protect". Add mod (against) to say from what: Vi beskytter huset mod regn (We protect the house against rain).

sentence.da: Du skal **beskytte** huden mod solen.
sentence.en: You need to protect your skin from the sun.

at beskæftige sig med.explanation: "At beskæftige sig med" means "to deal with" or "to work with": to spend your time on a subject or task. It is common for jobs and studies: Hun beskæftiger sig med sprog (She works with languages). Without sig, at beskæftige means "to employ": Firmaet beskæftiger 50 personer (The company employs 50 people).

forms.en: I have dealt with / worked with

sentence.da: Min bror vil **beskæftige sig med** klimaforskning i fremtiden.
sentence.en: My brother wants to work with climate research in the future.

at beslaglægge.explanation: "At beslaglægge" means "to confiscate". Police or customs officers do it, taking something because it is illegal or needed as evidence: Politiet beslaglagde bilen (The police seized the car).

sentence.da: Tolden kan **beslaglægge** ulovlige varer i lufthavnen.
sentence.en: Customs can confiscate illegal goods at the airport.

at beslutte.explanation: "At beslutte" means "to decide", and it is often followed by at and an action: Vi besluttede at blive hjemme (We decided to stay home). To say you made up your mind, add mig: Jeg har besluttet mig (I have made up my mind).

sentence.da: Vi skal **beslutte**, hvor vi vil spise i aften.
sentence.en: We have to decide where we want to eat tonight.

at beslutte sig.explanation: "At beslutte sig" means "to decide", or to make up your mind. To say what you chose, add for: Jeg besluttede mig for at blive (I decided to stay).

sentence.da: Hun skal **beslutte sig** inden i morgen.
sentence.en: She has to decide before tomorrow.

at bestemme.explanation: "At bestemme" means "to decide". It also means to be the one in charge: Hvem bestemmer her? (Who decides here?)

sentence.da: Du må **bestemme**, hvad vi skal spise.
sentence.en: You get to decide what we eat.

at bestemme sig.explanation: "At bestemme sig" means "to make up one's mind". Without sig, at bestemme means "to decide for others": Chefen bestemmer (The boss decides).

forms.en: I have made up my mind

sentence.da: Han skal **bestemme sig** i dag.
sentence.en: He has to make up his mind today.

at bestige.explanation: "At bestige" means "to climb" a mountain: you set out to reach the summit. It takes the thing directly, with no extra word: Hun bestiger Mont Blanc (She climbs Mont Blanc). At klatre (to climb) is for climbing with hands and feet, such as a tree or a wall.

sentence.da: Vi vil **bestige** bjerget og se solopgangen fra toppen.
sentence.en: We will climb the mountain and watch the sunrise from the top.

at bestille.explanation: "At bestille" means "to order" or "to book", for example food or a table: Jeg vil gerne bestille et bord (I would like to book a table). To ask for a meal, you can also say Jeg vil gerne have en pizza (I would like a pizza).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **bestille** en pizza.
sentence.en: I would like to order a pizza.

at bestille tid.explanation: "At bestille tid" means "to make an appointment", for example at the doctor, dentist or hairdresser. Literally, it is to book time: bestille (to book) and tid (time). To say who with, add hos (at / with): bestille tid hos lægen (make an appointment with the doctor).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **bestille tid** hos lægen.
sentence.en: I would like to make an appointment with the doctor.

at bestride.explanation: "At bestride" means "to dispute", to say that a claim is not true: Han bestrider tallene (He disputes the figures). It also means "to pay for", used for costs: Firmaet bestrider udgifterne (The company pays the costs).

sentence.da: Hun vil **bestride** anklagen, fordi den ikke er sand.
sentence.en: She will dispute the charge because it is not true.

at bestræbe sig.explanation: "At bestræbe sig" means "to strive", to try hard to achieve something. It is followed by på at (to) before another verb: Vi bestræber os på at svare hurtigt (We strive to answer quickly).

sentence.da: Man skal **bestræbe sig** på at være ærlig.
sentence.en: One must strive to be honest.

at bestå.explanation: "At bestå" means "to pass" a test: Hun bestod prøven (She passed the test). With af, it means "to consist of": Holdet består af ti spillere (The team consists of ten players).

sentence.da: Hun skal læse meget for at **bestå** eksamen.
sentence.en: She has to study a lot to pass the exam.

at besvare.explanation: "At besvare" means "to answer": you answer a letter, an email or a question directly: besvare et brev (answer a letter). Unlike at svare (to answer), it needs no på: svare på et brev.

sentence.da: Eleverne skal **besvare** alle spørgsmålene i prøven.
sentence.en: The students must answer all the questions in the test.

at besvime.explanation: "At besvime" means "to faint": to lose consciousness for a short time, for example from shock or hunger. To say someone has fainted, Danes use er (am/is), not har (have): Hun er besvimet (She has fainted).

sentence.da: I stærk varme kan man **besvime**, når man ikke drikker nok.
sentence.en: In strong heat you can faint when you do not drink enough.

at besøge.explanation: "At besøge" means "to visit". You put the person or place straight after it, with no word for "to": Jeg besøger Anna (I visit Anna). You can also say komme på besøg (to come for a visit).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **besøge** min mormor i dag.
sentence.en: I want to visit my grandmother today.

at betale.explanation: "At betale" means "to pay". Say what you pay for with for: Jeg betaler for billetten (I pay for the ticket). The amount comes straight after it: Jeg betaler hundrede kroner (I pay a hundred kroner).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **betale** 40 kroner for kaffen.
sentence.en: I have to pay 40 kroner for the coffee.

at betale af.explanation: "At betale af" means "to pay off", paying back money you owe in regular payments. The thing you owe comes after på (on): Vi betaler af på huset (We are paying off the house).

sentence.da: Vi kan **betale af** på lånet hver måned.
sentence.en: We can pay down the loan every month.

at betale for.explanation: "At betale for" means "to pay for". Here, for points to what the money buys: Jeg betaler for maden (I am paying for the food). With a person after it, you cover their share: Jeg betaler for dig (I am paying for you).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **betale for** kaffen.
sentence.en: I would like to pay for the coffee.

at betale med kort.explanation: "At betale med kort" means "to pay by card". Med means "with", so it is literally to pay with card. To pay in cash, say at betale kontant (to pay in cash).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **betale med kort**.
sentence.en: I would like to pay by card.

at betale sig.explanation: "At betale sig" means "to pay off", in the sense that something is worth the effort or the cost. It is almost always used with det (it): Det betaler sig at lære dansk (It pays off to learn Danish). It is not about paying money back.

forms.en: it has paid off (be worth it)

sentence.da: Gode sko er dyre, men det kan **betale sig**.
sentence.en: Good shoes are expensive, but it can pay off.

at betale tilbage.explanation: "At betale tilbage" means "to pay back": Jeg betaler pengene tilbage (I pay the money back). To say who gets it, put the person after betale: Jeg betaler dig tilbage (I pay you back).

sentence.da: Jeg har lånt penge og skal **betale tilbage**.
sentence.en: I borrowed money and have to pay back.

at betegne.explanation: "At betegne" means "to denote" or "to describe". It says what a word stands for: Ordet bil betegner et køretøj (The word bil stands for a vehicle). With som (as), it means to label something a certain way: Han betegnede det som en fejl (He labeled it a mistake).

sentence.da: Man kan **betegne** en ugle som en natfugl.
sentence.en: You can describe an owl as a night bird.

at betjene.explanation: "At betjene" means "to serve" and "to operate": to help customers in a shop, or to work a machine. Han betjener kranen (He operates the crane). For serving food at a table, use at servere instead.

sentence.da: Hun skal **betjene** kunderne ved disken, når de kommer.
sentence.en: She has to serve the customers at the counter when they come.

at betragte.explanation: "At betragte" means "to regard" and "to consider": you see someone or something as something else, with som (as) before it: Jeg betragter ham som en ven (I regard him as a friend). It can also mean to look at something calmly and for a while.

sentence.da: Mange vil **betragte** ham som landets bedste forfatter.
sentence.en: Many regard him as the country's best author.

at betro.explanation: "At betro" means "to confide", to tell something private to someone close to you. It is often used with sig and til (to): Hun betroede sig til sin søster (She opened up to her sister).

sentence.da: Man kan **betro** sine hemmeligheder til en god ven.
sentence.en: You can confide your secrets to a good friend.

at betvivle.explanation: "At betvivle" means "to doubt" or "to question", to not be sure that something is true or right. It takes the thing directly: Jeg betvivler hans ord (I doubt his word). The shorter at tvivle (to doubt) needs på (on) instead: Jeg tvivler på hans ord (same meaning).

sentence.da: Ingen kan **betvivle**, at hun har arbejdet hårdt.
sentence.en: No one can doubt that she has worked hard.

at betyde.explanation: "At betyde" means "to mean": Hvad betyder det? (What does that mean?). You answer with Det betyder (It means) and then the meaning. It can also mean "to matter": Det betyder meget for mig (It means a lot to me).

sentence.da: Hvad kan det ord **betyde**?
sentence.en: What can that word mean?

at beundre.explanation: "At beundre" means "to admire", to feel respect and delight for a person or for what they can do: Jeg beundrer hendes mod (I admire her courage). It is much stronger than at kunne lide (to like).

sentence.da: Jeg kan kun **beundre** hende, fordi hun aldrig giver op.
sentence.en: I can only admire her because she never gives up.

at bevare.explanation: "At bevare" means "to preserve", to keep something as it is so that it does not change. It is used for old buildings and traditions, and for staying calm: at bevare roen (to keep calm). To keep a thing you own, say at beholde instead.

sentence.da: Museet skal **bevare** gamle ting, så de ikke går tabt.
sentence.en: The museum has to preserve old things so they are not lost.

at bevilge.explanation: "At bevilge" means "to grant", to officially agree to give money for something. It is done by a council, a government or a board: Kommunen bevilgede penge til en ny bro (The council granted money for a new bridge).

sentence.da: Politikerne vil **bevilge** flere penge til skolerne.
sentence.en: The politicians want to grant more money to the schools.

at bevise.explanation: "At bevise" means "to prove", to show with facts that something is true: Hun beviste, at det var sandt (She proved that it was true). It is also used for showing a quality: at bevise sit værd (to prove your worth).

sentence.da: Man kan **bevise** en teori med forsøg og målinger.
sentence.en: You can prove a theory with experiments and measurements.

at bevæge.explanation: "At bevæge" means "to move" something, like a body part. To move yourself, add sig: Han bevæger sig langsomt (He moves slowly). To move house, use at flytte (to move).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **bevæge** min venstre arm.
sentence.en: I cannot move my left arm.

at bevæge sig.explanation: "At bevæge sig" means "to move" your own body. To move a thing or move house, use at flytte (to move): Jeg flytter bordet (I am moving the table).

sentence.da: Katten kan ikke **bevæge sig**, fordi den sidder fast.
sentence.en: The cat cannot move because it is stuck.

at bide.explanation: "At bide" means "to bite", cutting into something with your teeth. It works for people, animals and insects: Myggen bed mig (The mosquito bit me).

sentence.da: Hunden kan **bide** med sine skarpe tænder.
sentence.en: The dog can bite with its sharp teeth.

at bidrage.explanation: "At bidrage" means "to contribute", to give your share to something that many people work on. What you contribute to comes after til (to): Hun bidrager til forskningen (She contributes to the research).

sentence.da: Alle i klassen kan **bidrage** med lidt mad.
sentence.en: Everyone in the class can contribute some food.

at binde.explanation: "At binde" means "to tie" or "to bind": you fasten something with a lace, string or rope so it stays in place. Jeg binder håret op (I tie my hair up).

sentence.da: Vi skal **binde** hunden til træet.
sentence.en: We have to tie the dog to the tree.

at binde snørebånd.explanation: "At binde snørebånd" means "to tie shoelaces". It is built from at binde (to tie) and snørebånd (shoelaces), and the same verb works for other things: at binde et tørklæde (to tie a scarf).

sentence.da: Min lille datter kan allerede **binde snørebånd**.
sentence.en: My little daughter can already tie shoelaces.

at bistå.explanation: "At bistå" means "to assist", to give someone a hand with a task or a case, often as a professional: Revisoren bistår firmaet (The accountant assists the company).

sentence.da: En advokat kan **bistå** dig, når du går i retten.
sentence.en: A lawyer can assist you when you go to court.

at blaffe.explanation: "At blaffe" means "to hitchhike", to travel by asking drivers to take you along for free.

sentence.da: Vi har ingen bil, men vi vil **blaffe** til kysten.
sentence.en: We have no car, but we want to hitchhike to the coast.

at blande.explanation: "At blande" means "to mix". With sig added (at blande sig), it means to interfere: Bland dig ikke i det (Stay out of it).

sentence.da: Du skal **blande** mel og æg i en skål.
sentence.en: You have to mix flour and eggs in a bowl.

at blande sig.explanation: "At blande sig" means "to interfere", taking part where you are not wanted. Plain at blande means "to mix": Jeg blander mel og vand (I mix flour and water).

sentence.da: Han skal ikke **blande sig** i det.
sentence.en: He should not interfere in that.

at blegne.explanation: "At blegne" means "to fade", to lose color and become pale. It is said about things left in the sun and about a face that turns white from fear: Hun blegnede af skræk (She went pale with fear).

sentence.da: Gardinerne kan **blegne**, når solen skinner på dem hver dag.
sentence.en: The curtains can fade when the sun shines on them every day.

at blinke.explanation: "At blinke" means "to blink" with both eyes and "to wink" with one. Lights and stars can blink too: Stjernerne blinker (The stars are twinkling).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **blinke** med det ene øje.
sentence.en: I cannot wink with one eye.

at blive.explanation: "At blive" means "to become" and also "to stay": Han bliver læge (He becomes a doctor) and Jeg bliver hjemme (I stay at home). It is also used for what will happen: Det bliver godt (It will be good). At være (to be) only says what is true right now.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **blive** læge.
sentence.en: I want to become a doctor.

at blive bange.explanation: "At blive bange" means "to get scared". Blive (to become) shows the change from calm to scared. To say you are scared right now, use at være bange (to be scared). Add what scares you with for: bange for hunde (afraid of dogs).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **blive bange**, når det tordner.
sentence.en: I can get scared when it thunders.

at blive enige.explanation: "At blive enige" means "to agree", when two or more people come to the same decision, so it needs more than one person. To give your own opinion, say Jeg er enig (I agree).

sentence.da: Vi skal **blive enige** om en pris.
sentence.en: We have to agree on a price.

at blive forelsket.explanation: "At blive forelsket" means "to fall in love", and you add i for the person: Hun blev forelsket i sin kollega (She fell in love with her coworker). Being in love already is at være forelsket.

sentence.da: Jeg er ved at **blive forelsket** i hende.
sentence.en: I am falling in love with her.

at blive færdig.explanation: "At blive færdig" means "to finish", as in be done: Jeg bliver færdig klokken fem (I will be done at five). With a job title it means to graduate: Hun bliver færdig som læge (She is graduating as a doctor).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **blive færdig** før frokost.
sentence.en: I would like to be done before lunch.

at blive gammel.explanation: "At blive gammel" means "to grow old". Blive means "to become", so it fits other changes too: at blive kold (to get cold), at blive stor (to grow big).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **blive gammel** og rask.
sentence.en: I would like to grow old and stay healthy.

at blive gift.explanation: "At blive gift" means "to get married", the moment of marrying. To say you are already married, use at være gift (to be married). Add the person with med (with): at blive gift med ham (to marry him).

sentence.da: Vi skal **blive gift** i sommer.
sentence.en: We are going to get married this summer.

at blive glad.explanation: "At blive glad" means "to become happy", the moment you feel pleased. Add for (about) to say what pleased you: Jeg blev glad for kagen (I was happy about the cake). Jeg er glad (I am happy) is about how you feel now.

sentence.da: Hun vil **blive glad**, når hun ser gaven.
sentence.en: She will be happy when she sees the gift.

at blive hjemme.explanation: "At blive hjemme" means "to stay home". Blive means "to stay" here, and hjemme means "at home".

sentence.da: Syge børn skal **blive hjemme**.
sentence.en: Sick children have to stay home.

at blive indlagt.explanation: "At blive indlagt" means "to be hospitalized", to be taken into the hospital to stay there, often overnight or longer: Jeg blev indlagt med lungebetændelse (I was hospitalized with pneumonia). A person who only comes for a check-up is not indlagt.

sentence.da: Hvis du er meget syg, kan du **blive indlagt**.
sentence.en: If you are very sick, you can be hospitalized.

at blive optaget.explanation: "At blive optaget" means "to be admitted", to get a place at a school, a course or a club after applying: Hun blev optaget i klubben (She was admitted to the club). Careful, it can also mean to be recorded: Samtalen blev optaget (The conversation was recorded).

sentence.da: Hun håber at **blive optaget** på universitetet i København.
sentence.en: She hopes to be admitted to the university in Copenhagen.

at blive overrasket.explanation: "At blive overrasket" means "to be surprised". Add over (by) to say what surprised you: Hun blev overrasket over nyheden (She was surprised by the news).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **blive overrasket** på min fødselsdag.
sentence.en: I would like to be surprised on my birthday.

at blive rask.explanation: "At blive rask" means "to get better" after being sick. Rask means "healthy" or "recovered". To someone who is ill you can say God bedring! (Get well soon!).

sentence.da: Du vil snart **blive rask**.
sentence.en: You will soon get better.

at blive skilt.explanation: "At blive skilt" means "to get divorced" and describes the event. To say what someone is now, use fraskilt: Han er fraskilt (He is divorced).

sentence.da: Mine forældre skal **blive skilt** næste år.
sentence.en: My parents are going to get divorced next year.

at blive syg.explanation: "At blive syg" means "to get sick", the moment you fall ill. At være syg (to be sick) describes the state you are in afterwards.

sentence.da: Uden søvn kan man **blive syg**.
sentence.en: Without sleep you can get sick.

at blive til.explanation: "At blive til" means "to become" or "to turn into": Larven blev til en sommerfugl (The caterpillar turned into a butterfly). Til (into) names what it becomes, while plain blive goes with a description: Han blev træt (He got tired).

sentence.da: Vand kan **blive til** is.
sentence.en: Water can turn into ice.

at blive træt.explanation: "At blive træt" means "to get tired", the change from not tired to tired. To say you are tired right now, use at være træt (to be tired).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **blive træt** af at løbe.
sentence.en: I can get tired from running.

at blive udskrevet.explanation: "At blive udskrevet" means "to be discharged", to be allowed to leave the hospital when the treatment is over: Du bliver udskrevet i morgen (You will be discharged tomorrow). The same word is used for writing out a prescription: at udskrive en recept (to write out a prescription).

sentence.da: Efter en uge kan du **blive udskrevet** og tage hjem.
sentence.en: After a week you can be discharged and go home.

at blive uvenner.explanation: "At blive uvenner" means "to fall out", to stop being friends after an argument. It always takes two sides, and med (with) names the other person: Jeg blev uvenner med min nabo (I fell out with my neighbor).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **blive uvenner** med dig over penge.
sentence.en: I do not want to fall out with you over money.

at blive venner.explanation: "At blive venner" means "to become friends". It always uses venner (friends), never ven, because two or more people are involved: Maria og jeg blev venner (Maria and I became friends).

sentence.da: Jeg tror, vi kan **blive venner**.
sentence.en: I think we can become friends.

at blive vred.explanation: "At blive vred" means "to get angry", the moment it happens. Being angry for a while is at være vred: Han er vred (He is angry).

sentence.da: Han kan **blive vred**, hvis jeg kommer for sent.
sentence.en: He can get angry if I am late.

at blive væk.explanation: "At blive væk" means "to stay away" and "to go missing": Han blev væk fra mødet (He stayed away from the meeting). Min nøgle er blevet væk (My key has gone missing).

forms.en: I have stayed away / gone missing

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **blive væk** fra festen.
sentence.en: I do not want to stay away from the party.

at blokere.explanation: "At blokere" means "to block", to stop something from passing or working: at blokere døren (to block the door). It is also used for cards, accounts and phone numbers: Jeg har blokeret hans nummer (I have blocked his number).

sentence.da: En væltet lastbil kan **blokere** hele motorvejen.
sentence.en: A tipped-over truck can block the whole highway.

at blomstre.explanation: "At blomstre" means "to bloom", for flowers and trees that open. It can also mean doing well: Byen blomstrer (The town is thriving).

sentence.da: Roserne vil **blomstre** i juni.
sentence.en: The roses will bloom in June.

at blotlægge.explanation: "At blotlægge" means "to expose", to bring something into the open so it can be seen or becomes known. It is built like the English lay bare. It can be a physical thing or a hidden problem: Regnen blotlagde rødderne (The rain exposed the roots).

sentence.da: Undersøgelsen vil **blotlægge** fejl i systemet.
sentence.en: The investigation will expose errors in the system.

at bluffe.explanation: "At bluffe" means "to bluff", to pretend you have a strong hand, or know more than you do, so others believe you. It is used in card games and in everyday life: Han bluffer, når han siger, at han kan fransk (He is bluffing when he says he knows French).

sentence.da: Man skal kunne **bluffe**, hvis man vil vinde i poker.
sentence.en: You have to be able to bluff if you want to win at poker.

at blæse.explanation: "At blæse" means "to blow", for wind and for blowing with your mouth: Jeg blæser lysene ud (I blow the candles out).

sentence.da: Det kan **blæse** meget på stranden.
sentence.en: It can blow a lot on the beach.

at bløde.explanation: "At bløde" means "to bleed". To say which part bleeds, add fra (from): Hun blødte fra næsen (Her nose was bleeding).

sentence.da: Han faldt og begyndte at **bløde**.
sentence.en: He fell and began to bleed.

at bo.explanation: "At bo" means "to live" in the sense of where your home is. For being alive, use at leve (to live, be alive): Min farmor lever stadig (My grandmother is still alive).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **bo** tæt på skolen.
sentence.en: I want to live close to the school.

at bo sammen.explanation: "At bo sammen" means "to live together". Without sammen (together), Jeg bor i Aarhus (I live in Aarhus) just says where you live.

sentence.da: Vi vil gerne **bo sammen** i en lille lejlighed.
sentence.en: We would like to live together in a small apartment.

at bokse.explanation: "At bokse" means "to box", as a sport. A person who does it is en bokser (a boxer).

sentence.da: Min bror vil gerne **bokse** i en klub.
sentence.en: My brother would like to box at a club.

at booke.explanation: "At booke" means "to book", for a room, a table or a trip. It is close to at reservere (to reserve).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **booke** et bord til fredag.
sentence.en: I want to book a table for Friday.

at bore.explanation: "At bore" means "to drill", to make a hole in a wall or in wood. The power tool is en boremaskine (a drill).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **bore** et hul i væggen.
sentence.en: I have to drill a hole in the wall.

at bortføre.explanation: "At bortføre" means "to abduct", to take a person away by force, for example a child: Barnet blev bortført i går (The child was abducted yesterday). It is built from bort (away) and føre (to lead).

sentence.da: Forbryderne ville **bortføre** direktøren og kræve penge.
sentence.en: The criminals wanted to abduct the director and demand money.

at bremse.explanation: "At bremse" means "to slow down", and also "to brake" in a car or on a bike. It works for anything you slow down: Regnen bremser os (The rain slows us down).

sentence.da: Du skal **bremse**, når lyset er rødt.
sentence.en: You have to brake when the light is red.

at bringe.explanation: "At bringe" means "to bring", but it sounds a bit formal. In daily talk, Danes say Jeg tager kaffe med (I'm bringing coffee). Bringe still shows up in bringe i fare (to put in danger).

sentence.da: Han vil **bringe** gaven til dig i morgen.
sentence.en: He will bring the gift to you tomorrow.

at brokke sig.explanation: "At brokke sig" means "to complain" or "to grumble" about small everyday things: Han brokker sig over vejret (He grumbles about the weather). The little word over (about) names what bothers you.

sentence.da: Min bror plejer at **brokke sig** over maden.
sentence.en: My brother usually grumbles about the food.

at bruge.explanation: "At bruge" means "to use", for example a tool or a phone. It also means "to spend" money or time: Jeg bruger mange penge (I spend a lot of money). What comes after it tells you which meaning is meant.

sentence.da: Du kan **bruge** en kniv til brød.
sentence.en: You can use a knife for bread.

at bruge op.explanation: "At bruge op" means "to use up", so nothing is left. Op adds that idea of finishing, as in at spise op (to eat up) and at drikke op (to drink up). Plain at bruge (to use) only says you used something.

sentence.da: Vi må **bruge op**, hvad vi har i køleskabet.
sentence.en: We have to use up what we have in the fridge.

at bruge penge.explanation: "At bruge penge" means "to spend money". At bruge (to use) also means "to spend", so at bruge penge på noget is to spend money on something. Penge (money) is used without en or et (a).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **bruge penge** på en jakke.
sentence.en: I would like to spend money on a jacket.

at bryde.explanation: "At bryde" means "to break", mostly for promises, rules and silence: Han brød sit løfte (He broke his promise). Watch out: brød also means bread, as in et brød (a loaf).

sentence.da: Man må ikke **bryde** reglerne i spillet.
sentence.en: You must not break the rules of the game.

at bryde et løfte.explanation: "At bryde et løfte" means "to break a promise", when you do not do what you promised. Bryde is also used for rules: at bryde en regel (to break a rule).

sentence.da: Han vil aldrig **bryde et løfte**.
sentence.en: He will never break a promise.

at bryde loven.explanation: "At bryde loven" means "to break the law". Bryde (to break) also works with rules and promises: at bryde et løfte (to break a promise). For a cup or a toy that stops working, use at gå i stykker (to break).

sentence.da: Det er forkert at **bryde loven**, også når ingen ser det.
sentence.en: It is wrong to break the law, even when nobody sees it.

at brække.explanation: "At brække" means "to break (a bone)": Hun brækkede armen (She broke her arm). To vomit, add sig: at brække sig (to throw up): Han brækkede sig (He threw up). For a glass or plate, say at gå i stykker (to break): Glasset gik i stykker (The glass broke).

sentence.da: Pas på, du kan **brække** benet på isen.
sentence.en: Be careful, you can break your leg on the ice.

at brænde.explanation: "At brænde" means "to burn". A fire burns, and so can food and skin: Jeg brændte brødet (I burned the bread). Jeg brændte min hånd (I burned my hand).

sentence.da: Bålet kan **brænde** hele natten.
sentence.en: The campfire can burn all night.

at brænde ud.explanation: "At brænde ud" means "to burn out", both for a candle or fire that goes out when everything has burned, and for a person who is worn out from too much work: Han er brændt ud (He has burned out). Here ud means "until it is all used up".

sentence.da: Hvis du arbejder for meget, kan du **brænde ud**.
sentence.en: If you work too much, you can burn out.

at brøle.explanation: "At brøle" means "to roar", the deep, loud sound of big animals such as bulls. A person can also roar, in anger or with laughter: at brøle af grin (to roar with laughter).

sentence.da: Løver kan **brøle** så højt, at man hører dem langt væk.
sentence.en: Lions can roar so loudly that you hear them far away.

at bukke.explanation: "At bukke" means "to bow", to bend forward as a sign of respect, for example on a stage: Skuespillerne bukker for publikum (The actors bow to the audience). To bend down for something you dropped, add sig: at bukke sig (to bend down).

sentence.da: I Japan plejer man at **bukke** for hinanden.
sentence.en: In Japan people usually bow to each other.

at bukke sig.explanation: "At bukke sig" means "to bend down", to lower your body to reach something near the ground: Jeg bukker mig for at tage pennen (I bend down to get the pen). Without sig, at bukke means to bow.

sentence.da: Han kan ikke **bukke sig**, fordi han har ondt i ryggen.
sentence.en: He cannot bend down because his back hurts.

at burde.explanation: "At burde" means "ought to", much like "should": Du bør hvile dig (You ought to rest). It says what is a good idea or a duty, not an order.

sentence.da: Du **burde** sove mere, fordi du er træt.
sentence.en: You should sleep more because you are tired.

at byde.explanation: "At byde" means "to offer" and "to bid". To offer food or drink, add på: Må jeg byde på en kop kaffe? (May I offer you a cup of coffee?) For a bid, the amount comes right after: Jeg byder tusind kroner (I bid a thousand kroner).

sentence.da: På en auktion kan man **byde** på gamle møbler.
sentence.en: At an auction you can bid on old furniture.

at byde velkommen.explanation: "At byde velkommen" means "to welcome", for greeting guests or a group: Jeg byder jer velkommen (I welcome you). It sounds a bit formal, like in a speech.

sentence.da: Læreren vil **byde velkommen** til de nye elever.
sentence.en: The teacher wants to welcome the new students.

at bygge.explanation: "At bygge" means "to build", for a big thing like a house or a small thing like a birdhouse.

sentence.da: Man kan **bygge** et hus af træ.
sentence.en: You can build a house from wood.

at bygge om.explanation: "At bygge om" means "to rebuild" or "to convert", working on a building that already stands. Om adds the idea of doing something over in a new way, as in at lave om (to redo) and at flytte om (to rearrange).

sentence.da: Vi skal **bygge om** i køkkenet.
sentence.en: We are going to remodel the kitchen.

at bygge på.explanation: "At bygge på" means "to build on", or to add on: Vi bygger på huset (We are adding on to the house). It also means "to be based on": Filmen bygger på en bog (The film is based on a book).

forms.en: I have built on / added on

sentence.da: Vi vil **bygge på** huset, fordi vi får et barn.
sentence.en: We want to add on to the house because we are having a baby.

at bytte.explanation: "At bytte" means "to exchange" or "to swap", for example to get another size. It also works for swapping with someone: Vil du bytte plads? (Do you want to swap seats?)

sentence.da: Jeg vil **bytte** skjorten til en større.
sentence.en: I want to exchange the shirt for a bigger one.

at bære.explanation: "At bære" means "to carry", and also "to wear": Han bærer en tung kasse (He carries a heavy box). For clothes, Danes often say have på (to have on): Jeg har en jakke på (I am wearing a jacket).

sentence.da: Kan du **bære** min taske til bilen?
sentence.en: Can you carry my bag to the car?

at bøje.explanation: "At bøje" means "to bend", to make something curve or fold. To bend yourself down, add mig, dig or sig: Jeg bøjer mig (I bend down).

sentence.da: Du skal **bøje** knæene, når du løfter.
sentence.en: You have to bend your knees when you lift.

at børste tænder.explanation: "At børste tænder" means "to brush teeth". Danish says just tænder (teeth), with no word for my: Jeg børster tænder, while English says I brush my teeth.

sentence.da: Jeg skal **børste tænder** hver aften.
sentence.en: I have to brush my teeth every evening.

at bøvse.explanation: "At bøvse" means "to burp". The burp itself is en bøvs (a burp).

sentence.da: Babyen skal **bøvse** efter maden.
sentence.en: The baby has to burp after the meal.

bacon.explanation: "Bacon" means "bacon", salted pork cut in thin slices and fried. You count it in slices (skiver), not in pieces.

sentence.da: Jeg steger fire skiver **bacon** til morgenmad.
sentence.en: I fry four slices of bacon for breakfast.

badebukser.explanation: "Badebukser" means "swim trunks", the short pants that men and boys swim in. It is always plural, so one pair is et par badebukser (a pair of swim trunks).

sentence.da: Drenge har **badebukser** på, når de svømmer.
sentence.en: Boys wear swim trunks when they swim.

badetøj.explanation: "Badetøj" means "swimwear": swimsuits, swim trunks and other clothes you swim in. It is built from bade (to swim) and tøj (clothes). Like tøj, it is a group word for all the pieces together, so it has no plural.

sentence.da: Jeg tager **badetøj** og håndklæde med til stranden.
sentence.en: I am bringing swimwear and a towel to the beach.

badminton.explanation: "Badminton" means "badminton", spelled the same as in English. It takes the verb spille (to play): Vi spiller badminton (We play badminton).

sentence.da: Man spiller **badminton** med en ketsjer og en fjerbold.
sentence.en: You play badminton with a racket and a shuttlecock.

bag.explanation: "Bag" means "behind" and is always followed by a person or thing. On its own, use bagved (at the back): Katten sidder bagved (The cat is sitting at the back).

sentence.da: Barnet gemmer sig **bag** træet.
sentence.en: The child hides behind the tree.

bagage.explanation: "Bagage" means "luggage", all your bags and suitcases together. There is no plural, so bagager is not used. It is said ba-GAH-sheh. For one single bag, say en kuffert (a suitcase) or en taske (a bag).

sentence.da: Vi lander i lufthavnen og henter vores **bagage**.
sentence.en: We land at the airport and pick up our luggage.

bagefter.explanation: "Bagefter" means "afterwards". Compare efter maden (after the meal) with bagefter (afterwards): Vi spiser, og bagefter ser vi film (We eat, and afterwards we watch a film). Efter (after) needs a thing after it; bagefter stands alone.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser nu og vasker op **bagefter**.
sentence.en: I eat now and wash the dishes afterwards.

bagepapir.explanation: "Bagepapir" means "baking paper", the paper you put on a baking tray so the food does not stick.

sentence.da: Kagen sidder ikke fast, fordi jeg bruger **bagepapir**.
sentence.en: The cake does not stick, because I use baking paper.

bagepulver.explanation: "Bagepulver" means "baking powder", a white powder that makes a cake rise and turn out light.

sentence.da: Kagen hæver ikke uden **bagepulver**.
sentence.en: The cake does not rise without baking powder.

bagfra.explanation: "Bagfra" means "from behind", where something comes from or is seen from: Jeg så ham bagfra (I saw him from behind). The ending fra (from) works the same way in many direction words.

sentence.da: Cyklisten blev ramt **bagfra** af en bil.
sentence.en: The cyclist was hit from behind by a car.

baglæns.explanation: "Baglæns" means "backwards", with the back first or in reverse order. It tells how you move; to return to where you were, say tilbage (back): Gå tilbage! (Go back!)

sentence.da: Vi tæller **baglæns** fra ti, når raketten skal starte.
sentence.en: We count backwards from ten when the rocket is about to launch.

bagom.explanation: "Bagom" means "behind", with the idea of going around to the back. For a spot where something simply is, use bag (behind): Katten sidder bag døren (The cat sits behind the door).

sentence.da: Vi går **bagom** huset og kommer ind gennem køkkenet.
sentence.en: We go around the back of the house and come in through the kitchen.

bagt.explanation: "Bagt" means "baked", cooked in the oven, the way bread and cake are. Food cooked in a pan is stegt (fried), not bagt.

sentence.da: Jeg laver **bagt** laks i ovnen.
sentence.en: I make baked salmon in the oven.

bagud.explanation: "Bagud" means "behind", but in score, time or progress rather than position: bagud med huslejen (behind on the rent). For where something sits, use bag (behind).

sentence.da: Vi ligger **bagud** med to mål, men der er tid tilbage.
sentence.en: We are behind by two goals, but there is time left.

bagved.explanation: "Bagved" means "at the back". Compare Han står bag mig (He is standing behind me) with Han står bagved (He is standing at the back). With a thing after it, use bag.

forms.en: He is standing at the back.
The house is at the back.

sentence.da: Emma står **bagved** og ikke foran.
sentence.en: Emma stands at the back and not in front.

ballade.explanation: "Ballade" means "trouble" or "a fuss", usually loud trouble with people. A common phrase is at lave ballade (to make trouble).

sentence.da: Der er altid **ballade**, når børnene leger.
sentence.en: There is always a fuss when the children play.

balsam.explanation: "Balsam" means "conditioner" for hair, a cream you rub in after shampoo and rinse out again.

sentence.da: **Balsam** gør håret blødt og let at rede.
sentence.en: Conditioner makes hair soft and easy to comb.

bange.explanation: "Bange" means "afraid" or "scared". What you fear comes after for (of). Vær ikke bange means "Do not be afraid".

sentence.da: Jeg er meget **bange** i mørket.
sentence.en: I am very scared in the dark.

bange for.explanation: "Bange for" means "afraid of". It can also mean "afraid that": Jeg er bange for, at det er sandt (I am afraid it is true).

forms.en: She is afraid of the dark.

forms.da: Er du bange for at flyve?

sentence.da: Børnene er **bange for** mørket.
sentence.en: The children are afraid of the dark.

banko.explanation: "Banko" means "bingo", a game common in clubs and at community events, where the winner shouts Banko!

sentence.da: Til **banko** krydser vi tal af, når de bliver råbt op.
sentence.en: At bingo we cross off numbers when they are called out.

barberskum.explanation: "Barberskum" means "shaving foam", the foam you put on your face before you shave. It is built from barbere (to shave) and skum (foam), and the same skum is in et skumbad (a bubble bath).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger **barberskum**, når jeg barberer mig.
sentence.en: I use shaving foam when I shave.

bare.explanation: "Bare" means "just" or "only". It often makes a sentence softer: Det er bare mig (It is just me). In an invitation it is friendly and means "go ahead": Kom bare ind (Come on in).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **bare** sove i dag.
sentence.en: I just want to sleep today.

bark.explanation: "Bark" means "bark", the hard outer layer of a tree. It is not the sound of a dog: to bark is at gø.

sentence.da: Birkens **bark** er hvid og kan skrælles af i strimler.
sentence.en: The birch bark is white and can be peeled off in strips.

barmhjertighed.explanation: "En barmhjertighed" means "mercy", kindness shown to someone who is suffering or who deserves punishment. It is usually used alone with no en in front: vise barmhjertighed (to show mercy).

sentence.da: Han bad om **barmhjertighed**, men dommeren sagde nej.
sentence.en: He asked for mercy, but the judge said no.

barsel.explanation: "Barsel" means "maternity or parental leave", time off work when a child arrives. It is used for fathers too, not only mothers.

sentence.da: Min bror er på **barsel** og passer sin lille datter hjemme.
sentence.en: My brother is on parental leave and looks after his little daughter at home.

barsk.explanation: "Barsk" means "harsh", for cold, stormy weather and nature, and for a person or tone that is tough and blunt: Hun har en barsk stemme (She has a harsh voice).

sentence.da: Vinteren i Nordnorge er **barsk**, og vinden er iskold.
sentence.en: The winter in northern Norway is harsh, and the wind is ice cold.

basilikum.explanation: "Basilikum" means "basil", the herb used a lot in Italian food.

sentence.da: Vi plukker frisk **basilikum** til pizzaen.
sentence.en: We pick fresh basil for the pizza.

basketball.explanation: "Basketball" means "basketball", the team sport played with a big ball and a high hoop. The same word also names the ball: en basketball (a basketball).

sentence.da: Man kaster bolden i en kurv i **basketball**.
sentence.en: You throw the ball into a basket in basketball.

bedre.explanation: "Bedre" means "better". Use end (than) to compare: bedre end i går (better than yesterday). Jeg har det bedre means "I feel better".

sentence.da: Din nye cykel er **bedre** end den gamle.
sentence.en: Your new bike is better than the old one.

bedre sent end aldrig.explanation: "Bedre sent end aldrig" means "better late than never". Say it kindly when someone shows up late or finally does something: Tak, fordi du kom. Bedre sent end aldrig (Thanks for coming. Better late than never).

forms.da: Nå, men bedre sent end aldrig.
Han kom, og det er bedre sent end aldrig.
forms.en: He came, and better late than never.

sentence.da: Du kom for sent, men **bedre sent end aldrig**.
sentence.en: You came late, but better late than never.

bedring.explanation: "En bedring" means "a recovery", getting well again after being sick. It is also used for anything that gets better, such as the weather or the economy: en bedring i økonomien (an upturn in the economy).

sentence.da: Lægen ser en langsom **bedring** efter operationen.
sentence.en: The doctor sees a slow recovery after the operation.

bedst.explanation: "Bedst" means "best", the top one of all. It also says what you like most: Jeg kan bedst lide kaffe (I like coffee best).

sentence.da: Carl er **bedst** i klassen.
sentence.en: Carl is the best in the class.

bedst før.explanation: "Bedst før" means "best before". It is printed on food, which is often still fine for a while after that date. Fresh meat and fish say sidste anvendelsesdato (use-by date) instead.

forms.en: best before the end of June

sentence.da: Mælken er **bedst før** fredag.
sentence.en: The milk is best before Friday.

bedsteforældre.explanation: "Bedsteforældre" means "grandparents", the parents of your mother and father taken together. It is built from bedste (best) and forældre (parents), and one parent is en forælder (a parent).

sentence.da: Mine **bedsteforældre** er mine forældres forældre.
sentence.en: My grandparents are my parents' parents.

bedøvet.explanation: "Bedøvet" means "anesthetized" or "numb", after a doctor or dentist has given something that takes away feeling: Munden er bedøvet (The mouth is numb). It can also mean dazed, as after a shock: Hun var bedøvet af chok (She was stunned by the shock).

sentence.da: Tandlægen gav mig en indsprøjtning, og nu er min mund **bedøvet**.
sentence.en: The dentist gave me an injection, and now my mouth is numb.

begavet.explanation: "Begavet" means "gifted", having a natural talent, mostly for learning and thinking. For a talent in one art you more often say talentfuld (talented): en talentfuld pianist (a talented pianist).

sentence.da: Hun er **begavet** og lærte at læse som fireårig.
sentence.en: She is gifted and learned to read at four.

begge.explanation: "Begge" means "both" and is only for two. Compare Begge er her (Both are here) with Alle er her (Everyone is here, any number). Jeg kender dem begge to (I know both of them).

sentence.da: Mine to børn er **begge** hjemme.
sentence.en: My two children are both at home.

begrænset.explanation: "Begrænset" means "limited", with only a certain amount or a point where it stops. It belongs to en grænse (a border): a limit is where something ends.

sentence.da: Vi har kun **begrænset** tid, men vi kan nå en kop kaffe.
sentence.en: We only have limited time, but we can fit in a cup of coffee.

begær.explanation: "Et begær" means "a desire", a very strong wish for something, often money, power or another person: begær efter penge (desire for money). It is much stronger than an everyday wish to have something.

sentence.da: Hans **begær** efter magt gjorde ham til en farlig mand.
sentence.en: His desire for power made him a dangerous man.

behagelig.explanation: "Behagelig" means "comfortable" or "pleasant" and describes things that feel good. It also fits a voice or a temperature: en behagelig stemme (a pleasant voice), en behagelig temperatur (a pleasant temperature).

sentence.da: Sofaen er blød og **behagelig**.
sentence.en: The sofa is soft and comfortable.

behjælpelig.explanation: "Behjælpelig" means "helpful", but mostly in the set phrase at være behjælpelig (to be of service): Kan jeg være behjælpelig? (May I be of service?) A person who likes to help is hjælpsom (eager to help).

sentence.da: Kan du være **behjælpelig** med at finde min kuffert?
sentence.en: Could you help me find my suitcase?

beige.explanation: "Beige" means "beige", a light, sandy color like dry sand.

sentence.da: Sandet på stranden er **beige**.
sentence.en: The sand on the beach is beige.

bekendt.explanation: "Bekendt" means "familiar" or "known". The same word is also a person: en bekendt (an acquaintance) is someone you know a little, not a close friend.

sentence.da: Hendes stemme lyder **bekendt**.
sentence.en: Her voice sounds familiar.

bekvem.explanation: "Bekvem" means "convenient" or "comfortable", but it is often used about easy solutions: en bekvem undskyldning (a convenient excuse). For a comfortable chair, Danes say behagelig (pleasant): en behagelig stol.

sentence.da: Det er en **bekvem** måde at betale på.
sentence.en: It is a convenient way to pay.

bekymrende.explanation: "Bekymrende" means "worrying", describing the thing that makes you worried. The person who feels it is bekymret: Jeg er bekymret (I am worried).

sentence.da: Det er **bekymrende**, at så mange unge sover for lidt.
sentence.en: It is worrying that so many young people sleep too little.

belysning.explanation: "Belysning" means "lighting", the lamps and light that make a place bright, in a room or on a street. It can also mean that a subject is examined: en belysning af sagen (a closer look at the matter).

sentence.da: God **belysning** i gaden gør os trygge, når det er mørkt.
sentence.en: Good lighting in the street makes us feel safe when it is dark.

bemærkelsesværdig.explanation: "Bemærkelsesværdig" means "remarkable", worth noticing. It is built from at bemærke (to notice) and værdig (worthy), and it is used for results, achievements and facts that stand out.

sentence.da: Hendes udholdenhed er **bemærkelsesværdig**, når man tænker på hendes alder.
sentence.en: Her stamina is remarkable when you think of her age.

benzin.explanation: "Benzin" means "gasoline", which Americans often call gas. A diesel car needs diesel instead.

sentence.da: Min bil kører på **benzin**, ikke på diesel.
sentence.en: My car runs on gasoline, not on diesel.

beredvillighed.explanation: "En beredvillighed" means "a readiness", being quick and glad to help others: Hun viste stor beredvillighed (She showed great readiness).

sentence.da: Når man gerne og hurtigt hjælper, viser man **beredvillighed**.
sentence.en: When you help gladly and quickly, you show readiness.

berettiget.explanation: "Berettiget" means "justified", with good reasons behind it, and also "entitled", allowed to receive something: Du er berettiget til hjælp (You are entitled to help).

sentence.da: Hendes kritik var **berettiget**, fordi fejlen var tydelig.
sentence.en: Her criticism was justified because the mistake was obvious.

beruset.explanation: "Beruset" means "drunk" or "intoxicated", the formal word you see in police reports and news: en beruset bilist (an intoxicated driver). In everyday speech Danes say fuld: Han er fuld (He is drunk).

sentence.da: Det er forbudt at køre bil, når man er **beruset**.
sentence.en: It is forbidden to drive a car when you are drunk.

berømt.explanation: "Berømt" means "famous" and is stronger than kendt (well-known): Hun er berømt i hele verden (She is famous all over the world). Den er berømt for sin ost (It is famous for its cheese).

sentence.da: Hun er en **berømt** sanger i hele landet.
sentence.en: She is a famous singer all over the country.

beskadiget.explanation: "Beskadiget" means "damaged", used for things that have taken harm but can often still be used.

sentence.da: Bilen er **beskadiget** efter ulykken.
sentence.en: The car is damaged after the accident.

beskeden.explanation: "Beskeden" means "modest" and describes someone who does not brag: Hun er beskeden trods sin succes (She is modest despite her success). It can also mean small: en beskeden løn (a modest salary).

sentence.da: Hun er **beskeden** og snakker aldrig om sine succeser.
sentence.en: She is modest and never talks about her successes.

beskidt.explanation: "Beskidt" means "dirty". To say something got dirty, use blive (to become): Mine sko er blevet beskidte (My shoes have gotten dirty).

sentence.da: Man bliver **beskidt** af at lege i mudder.
sentence.en: You get dirty from playing in mud.

beskyttelse.explanation: "Beskyttelse" means "protection", something that keeps you safe from harm.

sentence.da: Solcreme giver **beskyttelse** mod solen.
sentence.en: Sunscreen gives protection from the sun.

beskyttende.explanation: "Beskyttende" means "protective", used for things that keep harm away and also for people who watch over others. It comes from at beskytte (to protect).

sentence.da: Han bruger **beskyttende** briller, når han saver i træ.
sentence.en: He uses protective goggles when he saws wood.

beslutsomhed.explanation: "En beslutsomhed" means "a determination", acting firmly without doubt once your mind is made up: Hun handlede med beslutsomhed (She acted with determination). It describes how a person acts, unlike en beslutning (a choice), which is the choice itself.

sentence.da: Hun tøvede ikke, men handlede med **beslutsomhed**.
sentence.en: She did not hesitate but acted with determination.

beslægtet.explanation: "Beslægtet" means "related", belonging to the same family or origin, for people, animals, languages and words: Katten er beslægtet med løven (The cat is related to the lion).

sentence.da: Ulven er tæt **beslægtet** med vores hunde.
sentence.en: The wolf is closely related to our dogs.

bestemt.explanation: "Bestemt" means "for sure" and also "certain": Han kommer bestemt (He is coming for sure). It can also point at one particular thing: Jeg leder efter en bestemt bog (I am looking for a certain book).

forms.en: I definitely do not want to

sentence.da: Det er **bestemt** en god idé.
sentence.en: That is definitely a good idea.

bestemt form.explanation: "En bestemt form" means "a form with the", the version of a word that says the: en hund (a dog) becomes hunden (the dog), et hus (a house) becomes huset (the house). Danish usually puts the on the end of the word instead of in front.

sentence.da: Ordet bilen er i **bestemt form**, men en bil er det ikke.
sentence.en: The word bilen is in the definite form, but en bil is not.

bestik.explanation: "Bestik" means "cutlery": the knives, forks and spoons you eat with. It is used for the whole set, so for one piece you name it: en kniv (a knife), en gaffel (a fork) or en ske (a spoon).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger **bestik** og tallerkener på bordet.
sentence.en: I put cutlery and plates on the table.

bestikkelse.explanation: "En bestikkelse" means "a bribe", money or a gift given to someone in power to get an unfair favor. Without en, it names the crime: Han blev anklaget for bestikkelse (He was accused of bribery).

sentence.da: Politiet mener, at manden tog imod **bestikkelse** fra firmaet.
sentence.en: The police believe the man took bribes from the company.

besvær.explanation: "Et besvær" means "trouble" or "a hassle", the effort or inconvenience that something costs you. It also turns up in polite phrases: Undskyld besværet (Sorry for the trouble) is said after asking someone for something.

sentence.da: Det er for meget **besvær** at rejse så langt for et møde.
sentence.en: It is too much trouble to travel so far for a meeting.

besværlig.explanation: "Besværlig" means "troublesome", costing a lot of effort. It can also describe a person who is awkward to deal with: en besværlig kunde (a demanding customer).

sentence.da: Vejen til hytten er **besværlig**, fordi den er stejl og mudret.
sentence.en: The road to the cabin is troublesome because it is steep and muddy.

beton.explanation: "Beton" means "concrete", the hard gray building material. It is the finished material, while cement is only one of the things it is made from. You usually say beton on its own, without en.

sentence.da: Gulvet i kælderen er lavet af **beton**.
sentence.en: The floor in the basement is made of concrete.

betydelig.explanation: "Betydelig" means "significant", mostly in the sense of large in amount or degree: en betydelig stigning (a considerable rise). To say that something has great meaning, use betydningsfuld (meaningful).

sentence.da: Hun har en **betydelig** indflydelse på beslutningen.
sentence.en: She has a significant influence on the decision.

betydningsfuld.explanation: "Betydningsfuld" means "significant", full of meaning and weight, built from betydning (meaning) and fuld (full). It is about something that matters for what comes after, while betydelig (considerable) is about amount.

sentence.da: Opfindelsen af trykpressen var en **betydningsfuld** begivenhed i historien.
sentence.en: The invention of the printing press was a significant event in history.

betænkelig.explanation: "Betænkelig" means "doubtful" or "worrying", for something that makes you uneasy about whether it is wise or safe: Jeg finder planen betænkelig (I find the plan doubtful).

sentence.da: Situationen er **betænkelig**, fordi floden stiger hurtigt.
sentence.en: The situation is worrying because the river is rising fast.

bevidst.explanation: "Bevidst" means "conscious" or "deliberate". About an act it means that it was done with intent: Hun gjorde det bevidst (She did it on purpose). With om (about), it means aware of something.

sentence.da: Han er **bevidst** om, at det kan være farligt.
sentence.en: He is aware that it can be dangerous.

bevidsthed.explanation: "Bevidsthed" means "consciousness", both being awake and being aware of something. Common phrases are at miste bevidstheden (to lose consciousness) and at komme til bevidsthed (to regain consciousness).

sentence.da: Efter ulykken kom han til **bevidsthed** igen.
sentence.en: After the accident he regained consciousness.

bevidstløs.explanation: "Bevidstløs" means "unconscious", not awake and not reacting, for example after a fall. The ending løs means without, as in hjælpeløs (helpless).

sentence.da: Efter faldet lå cyklisten **bevidstløs** på vejen.
sentence.en: After the fall the cyclist lay unconscious on the road.

bevismateriale.explanation: "Et bevismateriale" means "evidence", all the documents, photos and recordings collected to show what happened in a case. It names the whole collection at once: Politiet har indsamlet bevismateriale (The police have collected evidence).

sentence.da: Fotos, breve og optagelser er alt sammen **bevismateriale** i en retssag.
sentence.en: Photos, letters and recordings are all evidence in a trial.

bevæbnet.explanation: "Bevæbnet" means "armed", carrying something to fight with. What the person carries follows med (with): bevæbnet med et gevær (armed with a rifle).

sentence.da: Politiet sagde, at manden var **bevæbnet** med en kniv.
sentence.en: The police said that the man was armed with a knife.

beæret.explanation: "Beæret" means "honored", feeling that someone has shown you great respect: Jeg er beæret over at møde dig (I am honored to meet you). After beæret, over names what you are honored about.

sentence.da: Hun følte sig **beæret**, da kongen takkede hende personligt.
sentence.en: She felt honored when the king thanked her personally.

bifald.explanation: "Et bifald" means "applause", the sound an audience makes to show it liked something. It also means "approval" of an idea or decision: Forslaget fik bifald (The proposal got approval).

sentence.da: Efter koncerten fik orkestret et langt **bifald** fra publikum.
sentence.en: After the concert, the orchestra got long applause from the audience.

billedkunst.explanation: "Billedkunst" means "art", the school subject where pupils work with pictures and shapes. It also names visual art in general, as opposed to music or writing.

sentence.da: I **billedkunst** lærer børnene at tegne og male.
sentence.en: In art, the children learn to draw and paint.

billig.explanation: "Billig" means "cheap". It can mean a low price or poor quality, and the situation usually makes clear which is meant. In a shop, you can ask Har du noget billigere? (Do you have something cheaper?).

sentence.da: Maden er **billig**, kun tyve kroner.
sentence.en: The food is cheap, only twenty kroner.

biodiversitet.explanation: "Biodiversitet" means "biodiversity", the variety of living things in one place. A forest with many kinds of plants and animals has a lot of it, while a field with a single crop has little.

sentence.da: Skoven har stor **biodiversitet**, fordi der lever mange forskellige arter.
sentence.en: The forest has great biodiversity because many different species live there.

biologi.explanation: "Biologi" means "biology", the study of plants, animals and the human body. For a school class, you leave out en: Jeg er god til biologi (I am good at biology).

sentence.da: Vi lærer om dyr og planter i **biologi**.
sentence.en: We learn about animals and plants in biology.

biologisk.explanation: "Biologisk" means "biological", about living things and the science of them. It is also used for family by birth, as in biologiske forældre (biological parents), as opposed to adoptive ones.

sentence.da: **Biologisk** affald er rester af planter og dyr.
sentence.en: Biological waste is what is left of plants and animals.

bitter.explanation: "Bitter" means "bitter" for a taste like strong coffee: Kaffen er bitter (The coffee is bitter). It also fits a person who is still angry about something: Hun er bitter (She is bitter).

sentence.da: Kaffen er for **bitter** for mig.
sentence.en: The coffee is too bitter for me.

blandet.explanation: "Blandet" means "mixed", for things made of different kinds: en blandet salat (a mixed salad). It is also used for feelings: blandede følelser (mixed feelings).

sentence.da: Jeg køber **blandet** slik til børnene.
sentence.en: I buy mixed candy for the kids.

blandt.explanation: "Blandt" means "among" and is used with several people or things: Han er blandt de bedste (He is among the best). For just two things, use mellem (between): mellem huset og træet (between the house and the tree).

sentence.da: Katten gemmer sig **blandt** blomsterne.
sentence.en: The cat hides among the flowers.

blandt andet.explanation: "Blandt andet" means "among other things" and shows that your example is only one of several. It is often written bl.a.

forms.da: Vi talte blandt andet om musik.
forms.en: We talked about music, among other things.
She can swim, among other things.

sentence.da: Jeg købte **blandt andet** brød og ost.
sentence.en: I bought bread and cheese, among other things.

blank.explanation: "Blank" means "shiny": en blank overflade (a shiny surface). It also means "blank", like a page with nothing on it: et blankt ark (a blank sheet).

sentence.da: Bilen er **blank**, fordi jeg har vasket den.
sentence.en: The car is shiny because I washed it.

bleg.explanation: "Bleg" means "pale", mostly for a face or skin that has lost its color, for example from illness, fear or cold. It also fits washed-out colors: blege farver (pale colors).

sentence.da: Hun blev helt **bleg** i ansigtet, da hun hørte nyheden.
sentence.en: She turned completely pale in the face when she heard the news.
