blind.explanation: "Blind" means "blind", for someone who cannot see: en blind mand (a blind man). Someone who cannot hear is døv (deaf).

sentence.da: Han er **blind** og kan ikke se.
sentence.en: He is blind and cannot see.

blod.explanation: "Blod" means "blood". The d is very soft, so it sounds close to blo. It is often part of longer words: blodprøve (blood test) and blodtryk (blood pressure).

sentence.da: Lægen tager en prøve af mit **blod**.
sentence.en: The doctor takes a sample of my blood.

blodig.explanation: "Blodig" means "bloody", covered in blood or full of violence. Unlike English, it is not used as a mild curse: it describes real blood or a violent event.

sentence.da: Han fik en **blodig** næse, da bolden ramte ham.
sentence.en: He got a bloody nose when the ball hit him.

blodsukker.explanation: "Blodsukker" means "blood sugar", the amount of sugar in your blood. People with diabetes check it often with a small device, to see whether they need food or medicine.

sentence.da: Efter et stort måltid stiger mit **blodsukker**.
sentence.en: After a big meal my blood sugar rises.

blodtryk.explanation: "Et blodtryk" means "blood pressure", how hard your blood pushes against the walls of the vessels in your body. Doctors often check it, because a value that is too high can strain the heart.

sentence.da: Lægen måler mit **blodtryk** med en manchet om overarmen.
sentence.en: The doctor measures my blood pressure with a cuff around the upper arm.

blokeret.explanation: "Blokeret" means "blocked", when something is in the way or shut, so nothing can get through. It is also used for a bank card or account that has been stopped, often after a theft: Dit kort er blokeret (Your card is blocked).

sentence.da: Vejen er **blokeret** af et væltet træ.
sentence.en: The road is blocked by a fallen tree.

blomkål.explanation: "Blomkål" means "cauliflower". It is built from blomst (flower) and kål (cabbage), so it literally means "flower cabbage". En blomkål is one whole head, and plain blomkål is the vegetable in general.

sentence.da: **Blomkål** er hvid og ligner en lille blomst.
sentence.en: Cauliflower is white and looks like a small flower.

blond.explanation: "Blond" means "blond", a light yellow hair color. It describes the hair itself or the person who has it.

sentence.da: Min søster er **blond**, men jeg har mørkt hår.
sentence.en: My sister is blond, but I have dark hair.

blot.explanation: "Blot" means "merely" or "just". It also appears in wishes: Havde jeg blot vidst det! (If only I had known!).

forms.en: He is only ten years old.

sentence.da: Jeg ville **blot** sige tak.
sentence.en: I just wanted to say thanks.

bly.explanation: "Et bly" means "lead", the heavy, soft, gray metal. Do not mix it up with the English verb lead (to guide): that is at lede in Danish.

sentence.da: Gamle rør kan være lavet af **bly**, som er giftigt.
sentence.en: Old pipes can be made of lead, which is poisonous.

blå.explanation: "Blå" means "blue". Put lyse (light) or mørke (dark) in front to make shades: lyseblå means "light blue" and mørkeblå means "dark blue".

sentence.da: Himlen er **blå** i dag.
sentence.en: The sky is blue today.

blæsende.explanation: "Blæsende" means "windy", with strong wind blowing. It comes from at blæse (to blow), and "Det blæser" means "It is windy".

sentence.da: Det var en **blæsende** dag ved havet.
sentence.en: It was a windy day by the sea.

blæst.explanation: "Blæst" means "wind", the windy weather you feel outdoors.

sentence.da: Der er meget **blæst** på stranden i dag.
sentence.en: There is a lot of wind on the beach today.

blød.explanation: "Blød" means "soft", pleasant to touch. It also describes a quiet, gentle sound: en blød stemme (a soft voice).

sentence.da: Jeg sover godt i en **blød** seng.
sentence.en: I sleep well in a soft bed.

blødende.explanation: "Blødende" means "bleeding", for a person or a body part that is losing blood right now. It comes from at bløde (to bleed).

sentence.da: Pres på det **blødende** sted, indtil blødningen stopper.
sentence.en: Press on the bleeding spot until the bleeding stops.

bogstavelig talt.explanation: "Bogstavelig talt" means "literally", used when something is really true as said, not as a figure of speech. The opposite is billedligt talt (figuratively speaking).

sentence.da: Der var **bogstavelig talt** ingen mennesker på gaden, ikke en eneste.
sentence.en: There were literally no people in the street, not a single one.

bogstaveligt.explanation: "Bogstaveligt" means "literally", exactly as the words say, with no hidden meaning. It is mostly used about how you understand something. Bogstaveligt talt (literally speaking) is a common set phrase with a similar meaning.

forms.da: Du skal ikke tage det bogstaveligt

sentence.da: Små børn forstår ofte ord **bogstaveligt**, så ironi er svær for dem.
sentence.en: Small children often understand words literally, so irony is hard for them.

boligmarkedet.explanation: "Boligmarkedet" means "the housing market", the buying, selling and renting of apartments and houses, with the prices that go with it. It describes a whole country or city, not one single home.

sentence.da: Priserne på **boligmarkedet** er steget meget i København.
sentence.en: Prices on the housing market have risen a lot in Copenhagen.

boligstøtte.explanation: "En boligstøtte" means "housing benefit", money from the state that helps people with a low income pay for where they live. It comes in two forms: boligsikring (for most people) and boligydelse (for pensioners).

sentence.da: Staten giver **boligstøtte** til folk med lav indkomst og dyr husleje.
sentence.en: The state gives housing benefit to people with a low income and expensive rent.

boller i karry.explanation: "Boller i karry" means "meatballs in curry sauce", a classic Danish home-cooked dish of small balls of minced meat in a mild curry sauce. Here boller means meatballs, not the sweet buns that are also called boller.

forms.en: meatballs in curry sauce with rice
a portion of meatballs in curry sauce

sentence.da: Jeg laver **boller i karry** af hakket svinekød og serverer dem med ris.
sentence.en: I make meatballs in curry sauce from minced pork and serve them with rice.

bomuld.explanation: "Bomuld" means "cotton", the soft fiber from the cotton plant, used for T-shirts and towels.

sentence.da: Man dyrker **bomuld** i varme lande og laver tøj af det.
sentence.en: Cotton is grown in warm countries and clothes are made from it.

borgerservice.explanation: "Borgerservice" means "Citizen Services": the municipal office for practical matters like a health insurance card, a passport or registering your address. It is written with a capital B, like the name of an office.

forms.en: I have to go to Citizen Services.

sentence.da: Jeg skal have nyt pas på **Borgerservice**.
sentence.en: I need a new passport at Citizen Services.

bortset fra.explanation: "Bortset fra" means "apart from" or "except". It names the one person or thing that does not fit what you just said.

sentence.da: Alle kom **bortset fra** Lars.
sentence.en: Everyone came except Lars.

bravo.explanation: "Bravo" means "bravo" and is the same word as in English. Shout it to praise a performance or a good effort.

sentence.da: **Bravo**, det var en flot koncert!
sentence.en: Bravo, that was a great concert!

bred.explanation: "Bred" means "wide" or "broad", for how far something stretches from side to side: a road, a river, a smile.

sentence.da: Vejen er **bred**, ikke smal.
sentence.en: The road is wide, not narrow.

briller.explanation: "Briller" means "glasses" (for your eyes) and is only used in the plural. To wear glasses is at have briller på.

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke læse uden mine **briller**.
sentence.en: I cannot read without my glasses.

brint.explanation: "Brint" means "hydrogen", the lightest gas there is. It is also used as a clean fuel for cars and buses, since burning it gives only water.

sentence.da: Vand består af ilt og **brint**.
sentence.en: Water consists of oxygen and hydrogen.

britisk.explanation: "Britisk" means "British", from Great Britain. Do not mix it up with engelsk (English), which is about England and the English language.

sentence.da: Han bor i London og er **britisk**.
sentence.en: He lives in London and is British.

broccoli.explanation: "Broccoli" means "broccoli", a green vegetable with a thick stalk and many small tops.

sentence.da: **Broccoli** er grøn og ligner et lille træ.
sentence.en: Broccoli is green and looks like a little tree.

brugbar.explanation: "Brugbar" means "usable" or "useful", for something that works well enough for the job. Nyttig (helpful) says more: it gives real value, while brugbar only says that it can be used.

sentence.da: Cyklen er gammel, men den er stadig **brugbar**.
sentence.en: The bike is old, but it is still usable.

brugt.explanation: "Brugt" means "used" or "secondhand", for things that someone owned before you. It comes from at bruge (to use).

sentence.da: Jeg købte en **brugt** cykel på nettet.
sentence.en: I bought a used bike online.

brun.explanation: "Brun" means "brown". It is also used for a suntan: Du er blevet brun means "You have a tan".

sentence.da: Chokolade er **brun**, ikke hvid.
sentence.en: Chocolate is brown, not white.

brunede kartofler.explanation: "Brunede kartofler" means "caramelized potatoes", small boiled potatoes turned in caramel until they are golden and sweet. They are a traditional side dish for the Christmas roast.

sentence.da: Til julemaden laver vi **brunede kartofler** med sukker og smør.
sentence.en: For the Christmas meal we make caramelized potatoes with sugar and butter.

brutal.explanation: "Brutal" means "brutal", for violence that is rough and cruel. It is also used for honesty that is blunt and painful, as in brutal ærlighed (brutal honesty), and for events that feel harsh.

sentence.da: Filmen var **brutal**, og mange vendte blikket væk.
sentence.en: The film was brutal, and many looked away.

brændende.explanation: "Brændende" means "burning", something that is alight right now. It is also used for strong feelings and urgent matters: et brændende ønske (a burning wish).

sentence.da: De hentede børnene ud af det **brændende** hus og slukkede ilden.
sentence.en: They got the children out of the burning house and put out the fire.

brændstof.explanation: "Brændstof" means "fuel", for example for a car. It is built from brænde (to burn) and stof (material), and the same stof is in et sprængstof (an explosive).

sentence.da: Bilen bruger meget **brændstof** på motorvejen.
sentence.en: The car uses a lot of fuel on the highway.

brød.explanation: "Brød" means "bread". Et brød is one loaf, and plain brød is bread in general. With a number, it does not change: to brød (two loaves).

sentence.da: Jeg køber **brød** hos bageren.
sentence.en: I buy bread at the baker's.

buddhisme.explanation: "Buddhisme" means "Buddhism", the religion based on the teachings of Buddha. Danish writes the names of religions with a small letter, unlike English: buddhisme, but Buddhism.

sentence.da: I **buddhisme** er meditation en vigtig del af livet.
sentence.en: In Buddhism, meditation is an important part of life.

bukser.explanation: "Bukser" means "pants" or "trousers". Like English pants, it is always plural, so for one pair say et par bukser (a pair of pants).

sentence.da: Jeg har **bukser** og sko på.
sentence.en: I am wearing pants and shoes.

bulgur.explanation: "Bulgur" means "bulgur", cracked wheat that is boiled until soft.

sentence.da: Jeg laver en salat af **bulgur**, tomat og persille.
sentence.en: I make a salad of bulgur, tomato and parsley.

buttet.explanation: "Buttet" means "chubby", pleasantly soft and full, mostly about babies and small children. About an adult it can sound unkind.

sentence.da: Den lille baby er **buttet**, og hans arme er bløde.
sentence.en: The little baby is chubby, and his arms are soft.

bydemåde.explanation: "En bydemåde" means "imperative", the form of a word you use to give an order or make a request, like Kom her! (Come here!) or Hjælp mig! (Help me!). The word literally means "ordering way", from byde (to order) and måde (way).

sentence.da: Sætningen Luk døren! står i **bydemåde**.
sentence.en: The sentence Close the door! is in the imperative.

byg.explanation: "Et byg" means "barley", a grain that grows well in Denmark's cool climate. It is used for animal feed and for byggryn (pearl barley). Byg! is also the command "Build!", from at bygge (to build).

sentence.da: Man bruger **byg** til at lave øl.
sentence.en: Barley is used to make beer.

byplanlægning.explanation: "Byplanlægning" means "urban planning", deciding how a town or city grows: where roads, buildings and green areas go. It is built from by (town) and planlægning (planning), and it is mostly handled by the council.

sentence.da: God **byplanlægning** gør det let at gå og cykle i byen.
sentence.en: Good urban planning makes it easy to walk and bike in the city.

byttepenge.explanation: "Byttepenge" means "change", the money you get back when you pay more than the price. Like penge (money), it is always plural. It comes from at bytte (to exchange).

sentence.da: Du får 20 kroner i **byttepenge**.
sentence.en: You get 20 kroner in change.

både…og.explanation: "Både … og" means "both … and". Både goes before the first thing and og goes before the second. It joins two things of the same kind.

forms.da: både i dag og i morgen

sentence.da: Hun taler **både** dansk **og** engelsk.
sentence.en: She speaks both Danish and English.

bærbar.explanation: "Bærbar" means "portable", something you can carry. On its own, en bærbar means a laptop: Jeg har købt en ny bærbar (I bought a new laptop).

sentence.da: Min computer er **bærbar** og let at tage med.
sentence.en: My computer is portable and easy to take along.

bæredygtig.explanation: "Bæredygtig" means "sustainable", something that can continue without using up nature's resources. It is common in talk about food, fashion and energy. The word literally means "able to carry", from bære (carry) and dygtig (able).

sentence.da: En **bæredygtig** løsning kan holde i mange år uden at ødelægge naturen.
sentence.en: A sustainable solution can last for many years without destroying nature.

bæredygtighed.explanation: "Bæredygtighed" means "sustainability", the idea of living and producing without using up what nature gives. Companies, schools and countries often name it as a goal. It is the name for the idea behind bæredygtig (sustainable).

sentence.da: Eleverne lærer om **bæredygtighed** og om at passe på naturen.
sentence.en: The students learn about sustainability and about taking care of nature.

bønner.explanation: "Bønner" means "beans". The same word also means prayers (from en bøn, a prayer), so the sentence shows which is meant.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser **bønner** og majs til aftensmad.
sentence.en: I eat beans and corn for dinner.

børnepasning.explanation: "Børnepasning" means "childcare", looking after small children during the day while adults work. In Denmark the municipality arranges and partly pays for it.

sentence.da: Vi har brug for **børnepasning**, fordi begge forældre arbejder.
sentence.en: We need childcare because both parents work.

en baby.explanation: "En baby" means "a baby", someone only a few months or a year old.

sentence.da: Vores **baby** er to måneder gammel.
sentence.en: Our baby is two months old.

en babyalarm.explanation: "En babyalarm" means "a baby monitor", a device with two parts: a microphone by the baby and a receiver for the parents.

sentence.da: Med en **babyalarm** kan vi høre barnet, når vi er i stuen.
sentence.en: With a baby monitor we can hear the child when we are in the living room.

en babysitter.explanation: "En babysitter" means "a babysitter", someone who stays with kids for an evening.

sentence.da: En **babysitter** passer børnene, når vi er ude.
sentence.en: A babysitter looks after the children when we are out.

en bachelor.explanation: "En bachelor" means "a bachelor's degree", the first degree after high school, usually three years at a university. It never means an unmarried man; for that Danes say en ungkarl.

sentence.da: Efter min **bachelor** læser jeg videre til en kandidat.
sentence.en: After my bachelor's I keep studying toward a master's.

en backup.explanation: "En backup" means "a backup", a spare version of your files kept in case something breaks. To make one, say at tage en backup (to take a backup).

sentence.da: Jeg har lavet en **backup** af alle mine billeder.
sentence.en: I made a backup of all my pictures.

en badedragt.explanation: "En badedragt" means "a swimsuit", often the one-piece kind. For a two-piece, use en bikini (a bikini).

sentence.da: Jeg skal have min **badedragt** med til poolen.
sentence.en: I need to bring my swimsuit to the pool.

en bademåtte.explanation: "En bademåtte" means "a bath mat", the mat you step on when you get out of the shower. It is built from bade (to bathe) and måtte (mat), and bade also starts et badeværelse (a bathroom).

sentence.da: Husk at lægge en **bademåtte** foran badekarret.
sentence.en: Remember to put a bath mat in front of the bathtub.

en badestrand.explanation: "En badestrand" means "a bathing beach", a beach meant for swimming. It is built from at bade (to bathe) and strand (beach). Bade is also in et badeværelse (a bathroom).

sentence.da: Vi svømmer hver dag ved en lille **badestrand**.
sentence.en: We swim every day at a small bathing beach.

en badevægt.explanation: "En badevægt" means "a bathroom scale", used to check how heavy you are. It is built from bade (to bathe) and vægt (weight). Vægt on its own means weight: Hvad er din vægt? (What is your weight?)

sentence.da: Min **badevægt** viser, at jeg har tabt mig to kilo.
sentence.en: My bathroom scale shows that I have lost two kilos.

en bagagebærer.explanation: "En bagagebærer" means "a luggage rack" on a car roof, or "a bike rack" over the back wheel.

sentence.da: Min cykel har en **bagagebærer** til tasken.
sentence.en: My bike has a rack for the bag.

en bageplade.explanation: "En bageplade" means "a baking tray", a flat metal sheet with low edges for cookies and buns. Danes often cover it with bagepapir (baking paper) so nothing sticks.

sentence.da: Jeg lægger kagerne på en **bageplade** og sætter den i ovnen.
sentence.en: I put the cakes on a baking tray and put it in the oven.

en bager.explanation: "En bager" means "a baker", the person who bakes bread and cakes. Danes say Jeg går til bageren (I am going to the baker's), literally to the baker, when they mean the shop.

sentence.da: En **bager** laver brød hver morgen.
sentence.en: A baker makes bread every morning.

en baggrund.explanation: "En baggrund" means "a background", the part behind something in a picture. It also means a person's past: Hun har en anden baggrund (She has a different background).

sentence.da: Billedet har en blå **baggrund**.
sentence.en: The picture has a blue background.

en baggård.explanation: "En baggård" means "a backyard" in a city: the shared space behind apartment buildings. It starts with bag (back).

sentence.da: Børnene leger i en **baggård** mellem husene.
sentence.en: The children play in a backyard between the houses.

en baglygte.explanation: "En baglygte" means "a taillight", the red light at the back of a car. It is also used for the red light on the back of a bicycle.

sentence.da: Din **baglygte** er rød, men forlygten er hvid.
sentence.en: Your taillight is red, but the headlight is white.

en bagning.explanation: "En bagning" means "a baking", the act of baking, or what comes out of the oven in one go: dagens bagning (today's baking). It comes from at bage (to bake).

sentence.da: Efter **bagning** dufter hele huset af friske boller.
sentence.en: After baking, the whole house smells of fresh rolls.

en bagside.explanation: "En bagside" means "a back", the rear side of something, like a page or a card. It also means "a downside", the unwelcome part of something good: medaljens bagside (the flip side of the medal).

sentence.da: Skriv navnet på kortets **bagside**.
sentence.en: Write the name on the back of the card.

en baguette.explanation: "En baguette" means "a baguette", the long French bread with a crisp crust.

sentence.da: En **baguette** er et langt, tyndt brød fra Frankrig.
sentence.en: A baguette is a long, thin bread from France.

en bakke.explanation: "En bakke" means "a hill", a small rise in the land. It also means "a tray": Jeg bærer en bakke med kaffe (I carry a tray with coffee).

sentence.da: Det er hårdt at cykle op ad en **bakke**.
sentence.en: It is hard to bike up a hill.

en bakterie.explanation: "En bakterie" means "a bacterium", a single-celled living thing. Some make you sick, while others are helpful, for example in your gut.

sentence.da: En **bakterie** er for lille til at se uden mikroskop.
sentence.en: A bacterium is too small to see without a microscope.

en balance.explanation: "En balance" means "a balance", being steady or even. For the money in a bank account, use en saldo (a balance).

sentence.da: Det er vigtigt at finde en **balance** mellem arbejde og fritid.
sentence.en: It is important to find a balance between work and free time.

en balje.explanation: "En balje" means "a tub", a wide, open container, often plastic or metal, for holding water or laundry. It is not a bathtub, which is et badekar.

sentence.da: Hun vasker tøjet i en **balje** med varmt vand.
sentence.en: She washes the clothes in a tub with warm water.

en balkon.explanation: "En balkon" means "a balcony", a small platform with a railing that sticks out from an upper floor of a building.

sentence.da: Vores lejlighed har en lille **balkon** mod gaden.
sentence.en: Our apartment has a small balcony facing the street.

en ballet.explanation: "En ballet" means "a ballet", a stage show where trained performers move to music in set steps.

sentence.da: I en **ballet** fortæller danserne en historie uden ord.
sentence.en: In a ballet the dancers tell a story without words.

en ballon.explanation: "En ballon" means "a balloon", a thin rubber bag. To blow one up, use at puste en ballon op (to blow up a balloon). Op (up) goes after the thing, like in at ringe nogen op (to call someone up).

sentence.da: En **ballon** er fuld af luft.
sentence.en: A balloon is full of air.

en bamse.explanation: "En bamse" means "a teddy bear". It can also be a friendly word for a big, cuddly person: Han er en rigtig bamse (He is a real teddy bear).

sentence.da: Min datter sover med sin **bamse**.
sentence.en: My daughter sleeps with her teddy bear.

en banan.explanation: "En banan" means "a banana". Say it with the stress on the last part: ba-NAN.

sentence.da: Aben spiser en gul **banan**.
sentence.en: The monkey eats a yellow banana.

en bandage.explanation: "En bandage" means "a bandage", a strip of cloth wrapped around an injured body part to protect it or hold it still. For a small sticky one on a cut, Danes say et plaster (an adhesive bandage).

sentence.da: En **bandage** beskytter såret og holder det rent.
sentence.en: A bandage protects the wound and keeps it clean.

en bande.explanation: "En bande" means "a gang", a group of people who work together, usually to commit crimes. It can also be a friendly word for a group of friends: Hele banden kommer (The whole gang is coming).

sentence.da: Politiet har anholdt en **bande**, som stjal biler.
sentence.en: The police have arrested a gang that stole cars.

en bane.explanation: "En bane" means "a court" or "a field" for sports. It also means "a track" where runners run or trains go: Løberne står klar på banen (The runners are ready on the track).

sentence.da: Vi spiller fodbold på en ny **bane** ved skolen.
sentence.en: We play soccer on a new field by the school.

en banegård.explanation: "En banegård" means "a railway station". It is built from bane (railway line) and gård (yard). With hoved (main) in front, en hovedbanegård (a main station) is the big central station of a city.

sentence.da: Vi venter på toget på en stor **banegård**.
sentence.en: We wait for the train at a big railway station.

en bank.explanation: "En bank" means "a bank", where you keep and handle money. Danes say at gå i banken (to go to the bank).

sentence.da: Jeg sætter mine penge ind i en **bank**.
sentence.en: I put my money into a bank.

en bankkonto.explanation: "En bankkonto" means "a bank account". It is built from bank (bank) and konto (account). Other accounts are named the same way, such as en opsparingskonto (a savings account) and en lønkonto (a salary account).

sentence.da: Jeg har penge på min **bankkonto**.
sentence.en: I have money in my bank account.

en bankrådgiver.explanation: "En bankrådgiver" means "a bank adviser", the person at a bank who helps customers plan their money, for example when buying a home or borrowing.

sentence.da: Min **bankrådgiver** hjælper mig, når jeg skal låne penge.
sentence.en: My bank adviser helps me when I need to borrow money.

en barbermaskine.explanation: "En barbermaskine" means "an electric shaver". It is built from at barbere (to shave) and en maskine (a machine), the same maskine as in en vaskemaskine (a washing machine).

sentence.da: Han barberer sig hver morgen med en **barbermaskine**.
sentence.en: He shaves every morning with an electric shaver.

en barista.explanation: "En barista" means "a barista", a person trained to make and serve espresso drinks, such as lattes, behind a counter. Do not mix it up with en bartender, who mixes alcoholic drinks.

sentence.da: En **barista** er uddannet til at lave god kaffe.
sentence.en: A barista is trained to make good coffee.

en barndom.explanation: "En barndom" means "a childhood", the years when you are small. To say when, use i (in): I min barndom boede vi på landet (In my childhood we lived in the country).

sentence.da: Jeg tænker ofte på min **barndom** hos mormor.
sentence.en: I often think of my childhood at Grandma's house.

en barndomsven.explanation: "En barndomsven" means "a childhood friend", a friend from when you were small. It is built from barndom (childhood) and ven (friend), and barndom also appears in et barndomshjem (a childhood home).

sentence.da: Han er min **barndomsven** fra børnehaven.
sentence.en: He is my childhood friend from kindergarten.

en barnedåb.explanation: "En barnedåb" means "a christening", the church ceremony where a baby is named and welcomed into the Christian faith. Afterward, the family often holds a party with cake and coffee.

sentence.da: Ved en **barnedåb** får barnet sit navn i kirken.
sentence.en: At a christening, the child gets its name in the church.

en barnepige.explanation: "En barnepige" means "a nanny" or "a babysitter". It is built from barn (child) and pige (girl), but a barnepige can also be a boy or a man: Min bror er barnepige i aften (My brother is the babysitter tonight).

sentence.da: Vores **barnepige** passer børnene i aften.
sentence.en: Our nanny is looking after the children tonight.

en barnevogn.explanation: "En barnevogn" means "a baby carriage", where a small baby lies down. For an older child who sits up, Danes use en klapvogn (a stroller).

sentence.da: Hun skubber en **barnevogn** ned ad gaden.
sentence.en: She pushes a baby carriage down the street.

en bartender.explanation: "En bartender" means "a bartender", the person who mixes and serves drinks behind a bar, often cocktails. Danes also say en barmand (a barman).

sentence.da: En **bartender** blander drinks og skænker øl i baren.
sentence.en: A bartender mixes drinks and pours beer at the bar.

en base.explanation: "En base" means "a base" in two main senses: a place where soldiers or researchers live and work, and in chemistry, a substance that is the opposite of an acid. For the bottom of an object, Danes say bund (bottom) instead.

sentence.da: Soldaterne bor på en **base** tæt på grænsen.
sentence.en: The soldiers live on a base close to the border.

en bedrager.explanation: "En bedrager" means "a con artist" or "a fraud", a person who cheats others, especially out of money. Danish separates the person from the crime: the person is en bedrager, the crime is bedrageri (fraud).

sentence.da: En **bedrager** lyver for at få andres penge.
sentence.en: A con artist lies to get other people's money.

en bedrift.explanation: "En bedrift" means "an achievement" or "a feat", an impressive thing that someone has done, often hard or brave. It can also mean a business, especially a farm: en landbrugsbedrift (a farm business).

sentence.da: At bestige Mount Everest uden ilt er en stor **bedrift**.
sentence.en: Climbing Mount Everest without oxygen is a great feat.

en bedstefar.explanation: "En bedstefar" means "a grandfather" in general. In everyday speech, Danes usually say morfar (mother's father) or farfar (father's father), which tells you which side of the family he is on.

sentence.da: Min **bedstefar** er min mors far.
sentence.en: My grandfather is my mother's father.

en bedstemor.explanation: "En bedstemor" means "a grandmother" in general. In everyday speech, Danes usually say mormor (mother's mother) or farmor (father's mother). A short, warm form is bedste (grandma).

sentence.da: Min **bedstemor** er min fars mor.
sentence.en: My grandmother is my father's mother.

en bedømmelse.explanation: "En bedømmelse" means "an assessment", a judgment of how good or correct something is, such as a wine, a school paper or a risk.

sentence.da: Læreren giver en **bedømmelse** af, hvor god opgaven er.
sentence.en: The teacher gives an assessment of how good the assignment is.

en bedøvelse.explanation: "En bedøvelse" means "an anesthetic", a treatment that makes part of the body lose feeling so that a procedure does not hurt. A small area is treated with en lokalbedøvelse (a local anesthetic); for a full sleep during surgery, Danes say narkose (general anesthesia).

sentence.da: Tandlægen gav mig en **bedøvelse**, så det ikke gjorde ondt.
sentence.en: The dentist gave me an anesthetic so that it did not hurt.

en befolkning.explanation: "En befolkning" means "a population", all the people who live in a country, city or area. It is about people as a group; one person in it is en indbygger (an inhabitant).

sentence.da: Danmarks **befolkning** er næsten seks millioner mennesker.
sentence.en: Denmark's population is almost six million people.

en befrielse.explanation: "En befrielse" means "a liberation", being released from an enemy, a prison or a power. It also means a feeling of relief when a burden is gone: Det var en befrielse at aflevere opgaven (It was a relief to hand in the assignment).

sentence.da: Efter krigen fik landet sin **befrielse**, og folk dansede på gaden.
sentence.en: After the war the country got its liberation, and people danced in the street.

en begavelse.explanation: "En begavelse" means "a talent", natural mental ability that you are born with, not a skill learned by practice: en stor begavelse (a great mind). Compare et talent, which is used for a particular skill, like music.

sentence.da: Hendes **begavelse** viste sig tidligt, fordi hun kunne læse som treårig.
sentence.en: Her talent showed early, because she could read at age three.

en begivenhed.explanation: "En begivenhed" means "an event", something special or important that takes place.

sentence.da: Festivalen er en stor **begivenhed** i byen.
sentence.en: The festival is a big event in the town.

en begravelse.explanation: "En begravelse" means "a funeral", the ceremony for a person who has died.

sentence.da: Der er en **begravelse** i kirken på lørdag.
sentence.en: There is a funeral in the church on Saturday.

en begrundelse.explanation: "En begrundelse" means "a justification" or "a reason", what you say to show why you did or decided something. It is used when someone asks you to defend an answer or a choice, for example at school or at work.

sentence.da: Hvis du siger nej, skal du give en **begrundelse**.
sentence.en: If you say no, you must give a justification.

en begrænsning.explanation: "En begrænsning" means "a limitation", something that holds you back, such as a rule or too little time. It is built on en grænse (a border or limit).

sentence.da: Manglende plads er en stor **begrænsning** i en lille lejlighed.
sentence.en: A lack of space is a big limitation in a small apartment.

en begyndelse.explanation: "En begyndelse" means "a beginning", the first part of something: i begyndelsen af filmen (at the beginning of the film). It is built from at begynde (to begin).

sentence.da: Et eventyr har en **begyndelse** og en slutning.
sentence.en: A fairy tale has a beginning and an ending.

en begynder.explanation: "En begynder" means "a beginner", someone who is new at something. It comes from at begynde (to begin).

sentence.da: Jeg er kun **begynder**, men jeg lærer hurtigt.
sentence.en: I am only a beginner, but I learn fast.

en behandling.explanation: "En behandling" means "a treatment". It comes from at behandle (to treat). It can also mean the way someone is treated, as in dårlig behandling (bad treatment).

sentence.da: Hun er syg og får **behandling** på sygehuset.
sentence.en: She is sick and is getting treatment at the hospital.

en bekendt.explanation: "En bekendt" means "an acquaintance", a person you have met a few times but are not close to: Han er en bekendt, ikke en nær ven (He is an acquaintance, not a close friend). It can also mean "familiar": Det er en bekendt sang (It is a familiar song).

sentence.da: Jeg mødte en **bekendt** i byen.
sentence.en: I met an acquaintance in town.

en bekendtgørelse.explanation: "En bekendtgørelse" means "an announcement" or "a regulation", an official written notice. As a regulation, it is a detailed rule that a minister issues to apply a law.

sentence.da: Ministeriet har udsendt en **bekendtgørelse** om nye regler for taxaer.
sentence.en: The ministry has issued a regulation about new rules for taxis.

en bekymring.explanation: "En bekymring" means "a worry". In the same family are at bekymre sig (to worry) and Jeg er bekymret (I am worried).

sentence.da: Min største **bekymring** er pengene.
sentence.en: My biggest worry is the money.

en belastning.explanation: "En belastning" means "a strain" or "a burden", something that is hard to carry or put up with, for a body, a person or a machine. It can be physical, like heavy lifting for the back, or mental, like long days at work.

sentence.da: Lange arbejdsdage er en stor **belastning** for kroppen.
sentence.en: Long workdays are a big strain on the body.

en belønning.explanation: "En belønning" means "a reward", something you get for good work or a good deed.

sentence.da: Du får en **belønning**, når du er færdig.
sentence.en: You get a reward when you are done.

en benzinstation.explanation: "En benzinstation" means "a gas station", where you buy fuel for your car. It is built from benzin (gasoline) and station (station), the same station as in en politistation (a police station) and en brandstation (a fire station).

sentence.da: Tanken er næsten tom, og vi skal til en **benzinstation**.
sentence.en: The tank is almost empty, and we have to go to a gas station.

en beregning.explanation: "En beregning" means "a calculation", the careful figuring of an amount with numbers, such as a price, a tax or the time a trip will take. Do not mix it up with en regning (a bill).

sentence.da: Min **beregning** viser, at turen koster otte hundrede kroner.
sentence.en: My calculation shows that the trip costs eight hundred kroner.

en bersærk.explanation: "En bersærk" means "a berserker", an old Norse fighter who battled in a wild frenzy. The word lives on in the phrase at gå bersærk (to go berserk), which means to lose control in anger.

sentence.da: I de gamle sagaer kæmper en **bersærk** vildt og føler ingen smerte.
sentence.en: In the old sagas, a berserker fights wildly and feels no pain.

en berøring.explanation: "En berøring" means "a touch", the moment when one thing meets another, often soft or light: en blid berøring (a gentle touch). It names the single touch itself, while the action is at berøre (to touch).

sentence.da: Mimosaen lukker sine blade ved den mindste **berøring**.
sentence.en: The mimosa closes its leaves at the slightest touch.

en besiddelse.explanation: "En besiddelse" means "a possession", something that belongs to you. It is often used in the plural for a person's things: personlige besiddelser (personal belongings). In law it also means the act of having something: besiddelse af stoffer (possession of drugs).

sentence.da: Hans eneste **besiddelse** var en gammel cykel.
sentence.en: His only possession was an old bike.

en besked.explanation: "En besked" means "a message", or a piece of information someone passes on to you. Use at give besked (to let someone know) and at få besked (to be told).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **besked** til dig fra Anna.
sentence.en: I have a message for you from Anna.

en beskrivelse.explanation: "En beskrivelse" means "a description", words that tell what someone or something looks like or how it works. You find one on a product page, in a manual or in a job ad.

sentence.da: Politiet bad om en **beskrivelse** af manden, der løb væk.
sentence.en: The police asked for a description of the man who ran away.

en beskyldning.explanation: "En beskyldning" means "an accusation", saying that someone has done something wrong, often without proof. A common phrase is at komme med en beskyldning (to make an accusation).

sentence.da: En **beskyldning** uden beviser kan skade en uskyldig.
sentence.en: An accusation without proof can harm an innocent person.

en beskæresaks.explanation: "En beskæresaks" means "(a pair of) pruning shears", strong scissors for cutting back branches and stems. Danish treats it as one tool, like en saks (scissors), not as a pair.

sentence.da: Med en **beskæresaks** kan man klippe tykke grene af.
sentence.en: With pruning shears you can cut off thick branches.

en beslutning.explanation: "En beslutning" means "a decision", a choice you make after thinking. To make one, use at træffe (to make): Vi træffer en beslutning (We make a decision).

sentence.da: Det var en svær **beslutning** at flytte til udlandet.
sentence.en: It was a hard decision to move abroad.

en beslutningsproces.explanation: "En beslutningsproces" means "a decision-making process", all the steps and talks that lead up to a final choice. It is often used about companies, schools and politics.

sentence.da: En **beslutningsproces** tager tid, fordi mange skal høres.
sentence.en: A decision-making process takes time because many people must be heard.

en beslutningstager.explanation: "En beslutningstager" means "a decision-maker", a person who has the power to make the final choice, often in a company or in politics.

sentence.da: En **beslutningstager** har det sidste ord i sagen.
sentence.en: A decision-maker has the last word in the matter.

en bestemmelse.explanation: "En bestemmelse" means "a provision", one written point in an official text, such as a contract or a law. In a contract, each bestemmelse says what you may or must do.

sentence.da: I kontrakten står der en **bestemmelse** om, hvem der betaler.
sentence.en: The contract has a provision about who pays.

en bestilling.explanation: "En bestilling" means "an order", something you ask a shop or restaurant to prepare or send. It comes from at bestille (to order).

sentence.da: Din **bestilling** er sendt, og den kommer i morgen.
sentence.en: Your order has been sent, and it is coming tomorrow.

en bestseller.explanation: "En bestseller" means "a bestseller", a book, record or other product that sells very many copies. It is borrowed from English and is most often used for books.

sentence.da: Hendes bog blev en **bestseller** og solgte over en million eksemplarer.
sentence.en: Her book became a bestseller and sold over a million copies.

en bestyrelse.explanation: "En bestyrelse" means "a board (of directors)", the group of people who lead a company, a school or an association for the owners or members. Clubs and housing associations have one too.

sentence.da: Foreningen har en **bestyrelse**, som vælges hvert år.
sentence.en: The association has a board that is elected every year.

en besætning.explanation: "En besætning" means "a crew", the people who work on a ship or a plane. On a farm, the same word means the animals: en kvægbesætning (a herd of cattle).

sentence.da: En **besætning** arbejder på skibet, mens passagererne rejser.
sentence.en: A crew works on the ship while the passengers travel.

en besættelse.explanation: "En besættelse" means "an occupation" when an army takes over a country, and also "an obsession" when someone cannot stop thinking about something. Here "occupation" is never a job. In Danish history, besættelsen means the German occupation from 1940 to 1945.

sentence.da: Hans **besættelse** af tal tager al hans tid.
sentence.en: His obsession with numbers takes all his time.

en besøgende.explanation: "En besøgende" means "a visitor", someone who comes to a place for a short time.

sentence.da: Der er mange **besøgende** på museet i dag.
sentence.en: There are many visitors at the museum today.

en betaling.explanation: "En betaling" means "a payment", money given for something you buy or owe.

sentence.da: Vi har modtaget din **betaling**, tak.
sentence.en: We have received your payment, thanks.

en betalingsmetode.explanation: "En betalingsmetode" means "a payment method", the way you pay, such as cash or MobilePay (a Danish phone payment app). Shops and websites list the ones they accept.

sentence.da: Du skal vælge en **betalingsmetode**, før du kan købe varen.
sentence.en: You must choose a payment method before you can buy the item.

en betingelse.explanation: "En betingelse" means "a condition", something that must be true or done before something else can happen. It is not the condition of a thing like health or weather. For that, use en tilstand (a state).

sentence.da: Du får lånet på én **betingelse**: du skal betale til tiden.
sentence.en: You get the loan on one condition: you must pay on time.

en betjent.explanation: "En betjent" means "a police officer", a person who works for the police and keeps order.

sentence.da: En **betjent** arbejder for politiet og holder styr på trafikken.
sentence.en: A police officer works for the police and controls traffic.

en betragtning.explanation: "En betragtning" means "a consideration", a point you take into account when you think about a question, or a remark about it. The plural is common for someone's thoughts on a topic: Jeg har nogle betragtninger om sagen (I have some thoughts on the matter).

sentence.da: Prisen er en vigtig **betragtning**, når vi vælger et sted at bo.
sentence.en: The price is an important consideration when we choose a place to live.

en betydning.explanation: "En betydning" means "a meaning", what a word stands for. With stor (big) it means importance: Det har stor betydning (It matters a lot).

sentence.da: Jeg kender ikke ordets **betydning**.
sentence.en: I don't know the meaning of the word.

en betændelse.explanation: "En betændelse" means "an inflammation", a red, puffy and often sore area where the body fights an infection. It is also the everyday word for the infection itself: en betændelse i øret (an ear infection).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **betændelse** i halsen, så det gør ondt at synke.
sentence.en: I have an inflammation in my throat, so it hurts to swallow.

en beundrer.explanation: "En beundrer" means "an admirer", a person who looks up to someone for their talent or work. It can also mean someone secretly in love: en hemmelig beundrer (a secret admirer).

sentence.da: Hun er en stor **beundrer** af Karen Blixens bøger.
sentence.en: She is a great admirer of Karen Blixen's books.

en bevilling.explanation: "En bevilling" means "a grant", an amount of money that an authority or a fund approves for a purpose, such as research. It can also be an official permit: en bevilling til at sælge alkohol (a permit to sell alcohol).

sentence.da: Forskerne fik en **bevilling** på en million kroner til projektet.
sentence.en: The researchers got a grant of a million kroner for the project.

en bevægelse.explanation: "En bevægelse" means "a movement", either a motion of the body or a group working for a cause: en politisk bevægelse (a political movement).

sentence.da: Hun lavede en hurtig **bevægelse** med hånden.
sentence.en: She made a quick movement with her hand.

en bh.explanation: "En bh" means "a bra", a piece of underwear that supports the breasts.

sentence.da: En **bh** er en slags undertøj til kvinder.
sentence.en: A bra is a kind of underwear for women.

en bi.explanation: "En bi" means "a bee", a small flying insect. Bees are not wasps: en hveps (a wasp) is a different insect.

sentence.da: En **bi** summer rundt om blomsten.
sentence.en: A bee buzzes around the flower.

en biavler.explanation: "En biavler" means "a beekeeper", a person who looks after colonies and collects the honey. The ending comes from at avle (to breed or raise), so the job is about raising the colonies.

sentence.da: En **biavler** passer bikuber og sælger honning på markedet.
sentence.en: A beekeeper looks after beehives and sells honey at the market.

en bibel.explanation: "En bibel" means "a bible", a copy of the Christian holy book; with a capital letter, Bibelen is the book itself. It can also be a book that people treat as the final word in their field: Bogen er kokkenes bibel (The book is the chefs' bible).

sentence.da: En **bibel** består af Det Gamle og Det Nye Testamente.
sentence.en: A bible consists of the Old and the New Testament.

en bibliotekar.explanation: "En bibliotekar" means "a librarian", a person who works in a library and helps people find books and information. Do not mix it up with en boghandler (a bookseller), who sells books instead of lending them.

sentence.da: Spørg en **bibliotekar**, hvis du ikke kan finde bogen.
sentence.en: Ask a librarian if you cannot find the book.

en bid.explanation: "En bid" means "a bite" of food. Add the food after it: en bid brød (a bite of bread).

sentence.da: Vil du have en **bid** af min kage?
sentence.en: Do you want a bite of my cake?

en bidragyder.explanation: "En bidragyder" means "a contributor", a person who gives money, work or ideas to a shared project. The ending -yder comes from at yde (to provide).

sentence.da: Museet takker hver **bidragyder** til den nye udstilling.
sentence.en: The museum thanks every contributor to the new exhibition.

en bikini.explanation: "En bikini" means "a bikini", the two-piece swimsuit. For a one-piece, say en badedragt (a swimsuit).

sentence.da: På stranden har hun en rød **bikini** på.
sentence.en: On the beach she is wearing a red bikini.

en bil.explanation: "En bil" means "a car". At køre i bil means to go by car.

sentence.da: En **bil** har fire hjul og en motor.
sentence.en: A car has four wheels and an engine.

en bilist.explanation: "En bilist" means "a motorist", a person driving a car. It is bil (car) plus -ist, and -ist makes a word for a person in en turist (a tourist) and en pianist (a pianist).

sentence.da: En **bilist** skal altid holde tilbage for fodgængere.
sentence.en: A motorist must always yield to pedestrians.

en bille.explanation: "En bille" means "a beetle", an animal with six legs and a hard shell that covers its wings. A ladybug is a beetle too: en mariehøne.

sentence.da: En **bille** har et hårdt skjold på ryggen.
sentence.en: A beetle has a hard shield on its back.

en billedhugger.explanation: "En billedhugger" means "a sculptor", a person who carves or shapes figures out of stone, wood or clay. It is built from et billede (a picture) and at hugge (to chop), so it is literally someone who chops out an image.

sentence.da: En **billedhugger** laver figurer af sten og ler.
sentence.en: A sculptor makes figures out of stone and clay.

en billet.explanation: "En billet" means "a ticket" for a train, bus, film or concert. You say at købe en billet (to buy a ticket).

sentence.da: Jeg har købt en **billet** til toget.
sentence.en: I have bought a ticket for the train.

en billetautomat.explanation: "En billetautomat" means "a ticket machine", the machine at a station where you buy a ticket yourself. It is built from billet (ticket) and automat (machine).

sentence.da: Du kan købe en billet ved en **billetautomat**.
sentence.en: You can buy a ticket at a ticket machine.

en billetkontrollør.explanation: "En billetkontrollør" means "a ticket inspector", a person who checks tickets on trains and buses. It is built from billet (ticket) and kontrollør (inspector).

sentence.da: En **billetkontrollør** tjekker billetterne i toget.
sentence.en: A ticket inspector checks the tickets on the train.

en bilnøgle.explanation: "En bilnøgle" means "a car key", the key that starts your car.

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke køre, fordi jeg har mistet min **bilnøgle**.
sentence.en: I can't drive because I lost my car key.

en bilulykke.explanation: "En bilulykke" means "a car accident". It is built from bil (car) and ulykke (accident), and ulykke also appears in en arbejdsulykke (a work accident) and en flyulykke (a plane crash).

sentence.da: Der var en **bilulykke** på motorvejen i morges.
sentence.en: There was a car accident on the highway this morning.

en bilvask.explanation: "En bilvask" means "a car wash", a place with machines that clean your car.

sentence.da: Bilen er meget beskidt, og vi skal finde en **bilvask**.
sentence.en: The car is very dirty, and we have to find a car wash.

en bindestreg.explanation: "En bindestreg" means "a hyphen", the short line used to join words or word parts, for example in sort-hvid (black-and-white). The longer line is en tankestreg (a dash), which marks a pause in a sentence.

sentence.da: Man skriver en **bindestreg** i ordet S-tog.
sentence.en: You write a hyphen in the word S-tog.

en biograf.explanation: "En biograf" means "a movie theater", the place where you watch films. You say at gå i biografen (to go to the movies). Danes often shorten it to bio, as in gå i bio (go to the movies).

sentence.da: Vi ser en film i en stor **biograf**.
sentence.en: We watch a movie in a big movie theater.

en biografi.explanation: "En biografi" means "a biography", a book or movie that tells the story of a real person's life. When people write about their own life, it is en selvbiografi (an autobiography).

sentence.da: En **biografi** om Niels Bohr fortæller om hans liv.
sentence.en: A biography of Niels Bohr tells about his life.

en biolog.explanation: "En biolog" means "a biologist", a scientist who studies living things such as plants, animals and cells. The ending -log is on many Danish names for experts: en psykolog (a psychologist), en geolog (a geologist).

sentence.da: En **biolog** undersøger, hvordan dyr og planter lever sammen.
sentence.en: A biologist studies how animals and plants live together.

en birk.explanation: "En birk" means "a birch", a tree with thin, light-green leaves, common in Danish forests and parks. The wood is pale and is used for furniture and firewood.

sentence.da: Stammen på en **birk** er hvid med sorte pletter.
sentence.en: The trunk of a birch is white with black spots.

en bivirkning.explanation: "En bivirkning" means "a side effect", an unwanted effect that comes along with a treatment, such as a pill, besides what it is meant to do. The prefix bi- means "secondary", as in et bijob (a side job).

sentence.da: Træthed er en almindelig **bivirkning** af den slags medicin.
sentence.en: Tiredness is a common side effect of that kind of medicine.

en bjergbestigning.explanation: "En bjergbestigning" means "a mountain climb", the trip up a mountain on foot. It is built from bjerg (mountain) and bestigning (climbing up), and bjerg also appears in en bjergkæde (a mountain range).

sentence.da: Efter en lang **bjergbestigning** stod vi på toppen.
sentence.en: After a long mountain climb we stood on top.

en bjørn.explanation: "En bjørn" means "a bear": Bjørnen sover hele vinteren (The bear sleeps all winter). A polar bear is en isbjørn, built from is (ice) and bjørn.

sentence.da: En **bjørn** er stor og kan løbe hurtigt.
sentence.en: A bear is big and can run fast.

en blanding.explanation: "En blanding" means "a mixture", two or more things put together.

sentence.da: Dejen er en **blanding** af mel og vand.
sentence.en: The dough is a mixture of flour and water.

en blanket.explanation: "En blanket" means "a form" that you fill in, for example at the doctor's or the bank. To fill one in you say at udfylde en blanket (to fill in a form). Do not mix it up with en form, which means a shape.

sentence.da: Du skal udfylde denne **blanket**.
sentence.en: You have to fill in this form.

en ble.explanation: "En ble" means "a diaper", the soft pad a baby wears under its clothes. To change a diaper, say at skifte en ble.

sentence.da: Babyen har en våd **ble**.
sentence.en: The baby has a wet diaper.

en blender.explanation: "En blender" means "a blender", the machine for smoothies and soups.

sentence.da: Jeg laver en smoothie i min **blender**.
sentence.en: I make a smoothie in my blender.

en blikkenslager.explanation: "En blikkenslager" means "a plumber", a tradesperson who also works with sheet metal. The name comes from blik (tin plate), and the job covers gutters, roof edges and often water pipes.

sentence.da: Vi ringer efter en **blikkenslager**, fordi hanen drypper.
sentence.en: We call a plumber because the tap is dripping.

en blodprop.explanation: "En blodprop" means "a blood clot", a lump of blood that blocks a tube in the body. In the brain, en blodprop i hjernen means a stroke; in the heart, en blodprop i hjertet means a heart attack.

sentence.da: En **blodprop** kan stoppe blodet i en åre.
sentence.en: A blood clot can stop the blood in a blood vessel.

en blodprøve.explanation: "En blodprøve" means "a blood test", a small sample of blood that is checked. It is built from blod (blood) and prøve (sample, test). You say at tage en blodprøve (to take a blood sample).

sentence.da: Lægen vil tage en **blodprøve**.
sentence.en: The doctor wants to take a blood sample.

en blodåre.explanation: "En blodåre" means "a blood vessel" or "a vein", any tube that carries blood around the body. More exact words are en vene (a vein) for blood going to the heart and en pulsåre (an artery) for blood leaving it.

sentence.da: Når man skærer sig dybt, kan man ramme en **blodåre**.
sentence.en: When you cut yourself deeply, you can hit a blood vessel.

en blog.explanation: "En blog" means "a blog", a website where someone writes posts. The writer is en blogger (a blogger).

sentence.da: Min søster skriver en **blog** om sin hund.
sentence.en: My sister writes a blog about her dog.

en blok.explanation: "En blok" means "a notepad" and also "a block", a solid piece of something such as ice or wood. For an apartment building, Danes say en boligblok (an apartment block).

sentence.da: Man river et ark af en **blok**, når man har skrevet noget.
sentence.en: You tear a sheet off a notepad when you have written something.

en blomme.explanation: "En blomme" means "a plum", a soft sweet fruit with a stone inside. Do not mix it up with en blomst (a flower): Jeg spiser en blomme, men jeg køber en blomst (I eat a plum, but I buy a flower).

sentence.da: Denne **blomme** er sød og lilla.
sentence.en: This plum is sweet and purple.

en blomst.explanation: "En blomst" means "a flower". It appears in compound words such as en blomsterbutik (a flower shop) and en blomstervase (a flower vase).

sentence.da: Hun plukker en smuk **blomst** i haven.
sentence.en: She picks a pretty flower in the garden.

en blomsterbuket.explanation: "En blomsterbuket" means "a bouquet", flowers tied together in one bunch. Danes often shorten it to en buket.

sentence.da: Han kom med en **blomsterbuket** af røde roser til min fødselsdag.
sentence.en: He came with a bouquet of red roses for my birthday.

en blomsterhandler.explanation: "En blomsterhandler" means "a florist", a person who sells flowers and arranges them for gifts and parties. Danes also use it for the shop: Jeg går forbi blomsterhandleren (I am going past the florist's).

sentence.da: Jeg købte roser hos en **blomsterhandler** på hjørnet af gaden.
sentence.en: I bought roses from a florist on the corner of the street.

en blondine.explanation: "En blondine" means "a blonde", a woman with pale yellow hair. For a man or any person, use the plain word blond: en blond mand (a blond man).

sentence.da: Min søster er en **blondine**, og jeg har mørkt hår.
sentence.en: My sister is a blonde, and I have dark hair.

en bluse.explanation: "En bluse" means "a blouse", a light top for a woman or girl. Do not mix it up with en skjorte (a shirt).

sentence.da: Hun har en rød **bluse** på.
sentence.en: She is wearing a red blouse.

en blyant.explanation: "En blyant" means "a pencil", a wooden writing tool with a gray core, and its marks can be erased. To sharpen one, say at spidse en blyant (to sharpen a pencil).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver med en **blyant**.
sentence.en: I write with a pencil.

en blæksprutte.explanation: "En blæksprutte" means "an octopus" and also "a squid", a sea animal that squirts dark ink. An octopus is en ottearmet blæksprutte (eight-armed) and a squid is en tiarmet blæksprutte (ten-armed).

sentence.da: En **blæksprutte** sprøjter blæk ud i vandet, når den er bange.
sentence.en: An octopus squirts ink into the water when it is scared.

en blære.explanation: "En blære" means "a bladder", the body part that holds urine, and also "a blister" on the skin, for example after a burn: en brandblære (a burn blister). For a blister from a shoe, use et vabel (a friction blister).

sentence.da: Nyrerne laver urin, som samles i en **blære**.
sentence.en: The kidneys make urine, which collects in a bladder.

en blødning.explanation: "En blødning" means "a bleeding", blood that leaves the blood vessels, from a cut or inside the body. One you cannot see is en indre blødning (internal bleeding).

sentence.da: Tryk på såret, hvis du vil stoppe en **blødning**.
sentence.en: Press on the wound if you want to stop bleeding.

en bodega.explanation: "En bodega" means "a local bar", a small, simple neighborhood bar, not a fancy place. The word comes from Spanish.

sentence.da: På vores lokale **bodega** kender alle hinanden og drikker billig øl.
sentence.en: At our local bodega everyone knows each other and drinks cheap beer.

en bodylotion.explanation: "En bodylotion" means "a body lotion", a light cream for your whole body after a shower. To put it on, say Jeg smører mig ind (I rub lotion on myself).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger **bodylotion** efter badet, fordi min hud er tør.
sentence.en: I use body lotion after the bath because my skin is dry.

en bog.explanation: "En bog" means "a book", something you read, from a novel to a school book. The plural changes the vowel: to bøger (two books).

sentence.da: Man kan låne en **bog** på biblioteket.
sentence.en: You can borrow a book at the library.

en boghandel.explanation: "En boghandel" means "a bookstore", a shop that sells books. To borrow books for free, go to et bibliotek (a library) instead.

sentence.da: Jeg køber en roman i en **boghandel** i byen.
sentence.en: I buy a novel in a bookstore in town.

en boghandler.explanation: "En boghandler" means "a bookseller", the person who sells books, and in everyday speech also the shop itself: Jeg går forbi boghandleren (I am going past the bookstore). The more exact word for the shop is en boghandel.

sentence.da: En **boghandler** sælger bøger, men en bibliotekar låner dem ud.
sentence.en: A bookseller sells books, but a librarian lends them out.

en bogreol.explanation: "En bogreol" means "a bookcase". It is built from bog (book) and reol (open rack), and reol also appears in en vinreol (a wine rack).

sentence.da: Vi har brug for en større **bogreol** til alle bøgerne.
sentence.en: We need a bigger bookcase for all the books.

en bold.explanation: "En bold" means "a ball", a round thing used in sports and games. To play with one, say at spille bold (to play ball).

sentence.da: Man kan sparke og kaste en **bold**.
sentence.en: You can kick and throw a ball.

en bolig.explanation: "En bolig" means "a home" in the sense of a place to live. For the feeling of home, use et hjem (a home): Vi har et rart hjem (We have a lovely home).

sentence.da: Vi leder efter en billig **bolig** i byen.
sentence.en: We are looking for a cheap home in the city.

en boligblok.explanation: "En boligblok" means "an apartment block", a building with many homes. It is built from bolig (home) and blok (block), and bolig also appears in et boligområde (a residential area).

sentence.da: Der bor mange familier i en **boligblok**.
sentence.en: Many families live in an apartment block.

en boligforening.explanation: "En boligforening" means "a housing association", a non-profit organization that owns homes and lets them to its residents at fair prices. Residents vote on how it is run at meetings.

sentence.da: En **boligforening** ejer mange lejligheder og har en lang venteliste.
sentence.en: A housing association owns many apartments and has a long waiting list.

en boligkarré.explanation: "En boligkarré" means "a city block" of homes, usually buildings built in a ring around a shared courtyard. Older parts of Copenhagen have many.

sentence.da: Børnene leger i gården midt i en **boligkarré**.
sentence.en: The children play in the yard in the middle of a city block.

en bolle.explanation: "En bolle" means "a bun" or "a bread roll". In boller i karry (meatballs in curry) it means a meatball, so the meaning depends on the dish.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en **bolle** med smør.
sentence.en: I eat a bun with butter.

en bombe.explanation: "En bombe" means "a bomb". A bomb threat is en bombetrussel, built from bombe and en trussel (a threat).

sentence.da: Politiet fandt en **bombe** ved stationen.
sentence.en: The police found a bomb at the station.

en bon.explanation: "En bon" means "a receipt", especially the small paper one from the register. At the checkout you may hear Skal du have bonen med? (Do you want the receipt?).

sentence.da: Jeg betaler i kassen og får en **bon**.
sentence.en: I pay at the register and get a receipt.

en bonde.explanation: "En bonde" means "a farmer", someone who works the land and keeps animals.

sentence.da: En **bonde** står tidligt op og malker køerne.
sentence.en: A farmer gets up early and milks the cows.

en bonus.explanation: "En bonus" means "a bonus", extra pay or a reward on top of the usual, such as money from an employer after a good year or a discount for loyal customers.

sentence.da: Firmaet giver os en **bonus**, når året er gået godt.
sentence.en: The company gives us a bonus when the year has gone well.

en bordplade.explanation: "En bordplade" means "a tabletop" and also "a countertop" in a kitchen. It is built from bord (table) and plade (board).

sentence.da: Vi skal have en ny **bordplade** i køkkenet.
sentence.en: We need a new countertop in the kitchen.

en boremaskine.explanation: "En boremaskine" means "a drill". It is bore (to drill) plus maskine (machine). You use the verb like this: at bore et hul i væggen (to drill a hole in the wall).

sentence.da: Jeg skal bruge en **boremaskine** til at lave et hul.
sentence.en: I need a drill to make a hole.

en borg.explanation: "En borg" means "a castle", an old, strong building with thick walls, made to defend a place. For a grand royal residence, use et slot (a palace or stately castle).

sentence.da: I middelalderen byggede man en **borg** for at forsvare sig.
sentence.en: In the Middle Ages, people built a castle to defend themselves.

en borger.explanation: "En borger" means "a citizen", a person who lives in a country or town and has rights and duties there. Public offices also call everyone they serve borgere: Kommunen hjælper borgerne (The municipality helps the residents).

sentence.da: Hver **borger** over atten år må stemme ved valg.
sentence.en: Every citizen over eighteen may vote in elections.

en borgmester.explanation: "En borgmester" means "a mayor", the person who leads a town or city. The leader of a whole country is en statsminister (a prime minister).

sentence.da: Byens **borgmester** holder en tale i dag.
sentence.en: The town's mayor gives a speech today.

en bosætning.explanation: "En bosætning" means "a settlement", a place where people come to live, or the act of making a home somewhere new. The first part, bo, is the same as in at bo (to live).

sentence.da: Ved åen opstod en **bosætning**, hvor folk byggede de første huse.
sentence.en: By the stream, a settlement arose where people built the first houses.

en botanisk have.explanation: "En botanisk have" means "a botanical garden", a place where plants are labeled with their names and grown for research as well as for visitors. The big one in Copenhagen is called Botanisk Have.

sentence.da: I en **botanisk have** kan man se planter fra hele verden.
sentence.en: In a botanical garden you can see plants from all over the world.

en bowlinghal.explanation: "En bowlinghal" means "a bowling alley", a place with lanes where you roll a ball at pins.

sentence.da: Der er en **bowlinghal** i byen, hvor man kan spille bowling.
sentence.en: There is a bowling alley in town where you can play bowling.

en bradepande.explanation: "En bradepande" means "a roasting pan", a wide, shallow pan for the oven, used for roasts, potatoes and vegetables. Do not mix it up with en stegepande (a frying pan), which goes on the stove.

sentence.da: Jeg lægger kartoflerne i en **bradepande** og sætter dem i ovnen.
sentence.en: I put the potatoes in a roasting pan and place them in the oven.

en branche.explanation: "En branche" means "an industry" or "a line of business", a field of work such as tourism or construction. You use it to say where you work: Hun arbejder i it-branchen (She works in the IT industry).

sentence.da: Min bror har arbejdet i den samme **branche** i ti år.
sentence.en: My brother has worked in the same line of business for ten years.

en brand.explanation: "En brand" means "a fire" that is out of control: Der er brand i huset (There is a fire in the house). For a campfire, say et bål (a campfire).

sentence.da: Der var en stor **brand** i byen i nat.
sentence.en: There was a big fire in town last night.

en brandalarm.explanation: "En brandalarm" means "a fire alarm", the loud signal that warns of fire: Brandalarmen går (The fire alarm is going off). It is built from brand (fire) and alarm (alarm).

sentence.da: En **brandalarm** ringer højt, når der er røg.
sentence.en: A fire alarm rings loudly when there is smoke.

en brandbil.explanation: "En brandbil" means "a fire truck", the big red truck that goes to fires.

sentence.da: Der er ild i huset, og en **brandbil** kommer.
sentence.en: There is a fire in the house, and a fire truck is coming.

en brandmand.explanation: "En brandmand" means "a firefighter", a person who puts out fires.

sentence.da: En **brandmand** redder folk fra et brændende hus.
sentence.en: A firefighter rescues people from a burning house.

en brandslukker.explanation: "En brandslukker" means "a fire extinguisher". It is built from brand (fire) and at slukke (to put out), and at slukke also means to switch off: at slukke lyset (to turn off the light).

sentence.da: Brug en **brandslukker**, hvis det brænder.
sentence.en: Use a fire extinguisher if something is burning.

en brandstation.explanation: "En brandstation" means "a fire station", the building where firefighters and their trucks wait for emergency calls. It is built from brand (fire) and station (station).

sentence.da: Brandbilen holder foran den lille **brandstation**.
sentence.en: The fire truck is parked in front of the small fire station.

en brandtrappe.explanation: "En brandtrappe" means "a fire escape", stairs that lead out of a building when the normal way is blocked, often on the outside wall.

sentence.da: En **brandtrappe** bruges, når den almindelige trappe er spærret af ild.
sentence.en: A fire escape is used when the ordinary stairs are blocked by fire.

en bredde.explanation: "En bredde" means "a width", how far something measures from side to side. Length and width are often said together: længde og bredde (length and width).

sentence.da: Vinduet har en **bredde** på to meter.
sentence.en: The window has a width of two meters.

en bregne.explanation: "En bregne" means "a fern", a green plant with feathery leaves. It has no flowers, and it spreads with tiny spores. It likes shade and damp ground.

sentence.da: I skoven vokser der en **bregne** med lange, fine blade.
sentence.en: In the forest there grows a fern with long, fine leaves.

en bremse.explanation: "En bremse" means "a brake", the part that slows a car or a bike. The same word is also the action: at bremse (to brake).

sentence.da: En **bremse** får bilen til at stoppe.
sentence.en: A brake makes the car stop.

en brevkasse.explanation: "En brevkasse" means "a mailbox", the box where letters are delivered. It also means "an advice column", where readers send in questions about life and love and an expert answers.

sentence.da: Læserne sender deres spørgsmål til avisens **brevkasse** og får råd.
sentence.en: The readers send their questions to the paper's advice column and get advice.

en brevsprække.explanation: "En brevsprække" means "a mail slot", the narrow opening in a door with a flap, where the mail is pushed through. It is built from brev (letter) and sprække (slit).

sentence.da: Posten falder på gulvet gennem en **brevsprække**.
sentence.en: The mail falls onto the floor through a mail slot.

en brik.explanation: "En brik" means "a game piece" or "a tile", a small piece you move or place in a game. A tile in Scrabble is en scrabblebrik (a Scrabble tile).

sentence.da: Spilleren flytter en **brik** hen over brættet.
sentence.en: The player moves a piece across the board.

en brise.explanation: "En brise" means "a breeze", a light, gentle wind that is usually pleasant, for example by the sea.

sentence.da: Der kommer en let **brise** ind fra havet.
sentence.en: A light breeze comes in from the sea.

en brite.explanation: "En brite" means "a Brit", a person from Great Britain. Nationality words are not capitalized in Danish, so brite starts with a small b. The country is Storbritannien (Great Britain).

sentence.da: En **brite** kan komme fra England, Skotland eller Wales.
sentence.en: A Brit can come from England, Scotland or Wales.

en bro.explanation: "En bro" means "a bridge", something you cross over a river, road or sea.

sentence.da: Vi går over en **bro** over vandet.
sentence.en: We walk over a bridge over the water.

en brochure.explanation: "En brochure" means "a brochure", a small printed booklet with information, for example from a hotel or a travel company.

sentence.da: Hotellet sendte mig en **brochure** med mange billeder.
sentence.en: The hotel sent me a brochure with many pictures.

en bror.explanation: "En bror" means "a brother". Danish has separate words for older and younger: storebror (big brother) and lillebror (little brother), as in Min lillebror er fem år (My little brother is five years old).

sentence.da: Min **bror** og jeg har samme mor.
sentence.en: My brother and I have the same mother.

en brownie.explanation: "En brownie" means "a brownie", a small, dense chocolate cake that is cut into squares. It is often served warm.

sentence.da: En **brownie** er en kage med meget chokolade.
sentence.en: A brownie is a cake with a lot of chocolate.

en browser.explanation: "En browser" means "a browser", the program you use to open web pages.

sentence.da: Jeg åbner min **browser** og søger efter opskriften.
sentence.en: I open my browser and search for the recipe.

en brudekjole.explanation: "En brudekjole" means "a wedding dress", the dress a bride wears for the ceremony. The word is built from en brud (a bride) and en kjole (a dress).

sentence.da: Til brylluppet har bruden en hvid **brudekjole** på.
sentence.en: At the wedding, the bride is wearing a white wedding dress.

en brudepige.explanation: "En brudepige" means "a bridesmaid", a girl or woman who helps the bride on the wedding day.

related.en: a best man / maid of honor

sentence.da: Min søster skal være **brudepige** til brylluppet.
sentence.en: My sister is going to be a bridesmaid at the wedding.

en brudgom.explanation: "En brudgom" means "a groom", the man who is getting married. The couple together are et brudepar (a bridal couple).

related.en: a best man / maid of honor

sentence.da: Han er en glad **brudgom** på sin bryllupsdag.
sentence.en: He is a happy groom on his wedding day.

en bruger.explanation: "En bruger" means "a user", a person who uses an app, a website or a service. It is built from at bruge (to use), which also means to spend: at bruge penge (to spend money).

sentence.da: Hver **bruger** har sin egen adgangskode.
sentence.en: Every user has their own password.

en brugsanvisning.explanation: "En brugsanvisning" means "a user manual", the paper that explains how to use a product.

sentence.da: Jeg læser en **brugsanvisning**, fordi maskinen er ny.
sentence.en: I am reading a user manual because the machine is new.

en brunch.explanation: "En brunch" means "a brunch", a big breakfast eaten late in the morning. A normal early breakfast is morgenmad (breakfast).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **brunch** sent om søndagen.
sentence.en: We eat brunch late on Sundays.

en brunkage.explanation: "En brunkage" means "a Danish spice cookie", a thin, dark cookie that Danes bake for Christmas. The dough is rolled out and cut into shapes.

sentence.da: En **brunkage** smager af kanel, nelliker og sirup.
sentence.en: A brunkage tastes of cinnamon, cloves and syrup.

en brunsviger.explanation: "En brunsviger" means "a Funen brown-sugar cake". It comes from the island of Funen (Fyn) but is now eaten all over Denmark, often with coffee.

sentence.da: En **brunsviger** er en blød gærkage med sukker og smør på toppen.
sentence.en: A brunsviger is a soft yeast cake with sugar and butter on top.

en bruser.explanation: "En bruser" means "a shower", the fixture you stand under. With a badekar (bathtub) you lie down instead.

sentence.da: Der er en ny **bruser** på badeværelset.
sentence.en: There is a new shower in the bathroom.

en bryllupsdag.explanation: "En bryllupsdag" means "a wedding anniversary", the day each year when a couple married. It is built from bryllup (wedding) and dag (day), and bryllup also appears in en bryllupsgave (a wedding gift) and en bryllupsfest (a wedding party).

sentence.da: I dag er det vores **bryllupsdag**, og vi spiser ude.
sentence.en: Today is our wedding anniversary, and we are eating out.

en bryllupsrejse.explanation: "En bryllupsrejse" means "a honeymoon", the journey a couple takes after the wedding. It is built from bryllup (wedding) and rejse (journey), and rejse is also a verb: at rejse (to travel).

sentence.da: Vi vil på **bryllupsrejse** til Italien i maj.
sentence.en: We want to go on our honeymoon to Italy in May.

en brændenælde.explanation: "En brændenælde" means "a stinging nettle", a wild plant whose leaves sting the skin when you touch them. It is often shortened to en nælde.

sentence.da: Hvis du rører ved en **brændenælde**, svier huden.
sentence.en: If you touch a stinging nettle, the skin stings.

en brødkniv.explanation: "En brødkniv" means "a bread knife", the long knife with small teeth that cuts bread without crushing it.

sentence.da: Han skærer det friske brød med en **brødkniv**.
sentence.en: He cuts the fresh bread with a bread knife.

en brødkurv.explanation: "En brødkurv" means "a bread basket", a basket for bread or rolls that stands on the table at a meal. It is built from brød (bread) and kurv (basket).

sentence.da: Vi lægger brødet i en **brødkurv**.
sentence.en: We put the bread in a bread basket.

en brødrister.explanation: "En brødrister" means "a toaster". It is built from brød (bread) and at riste (to toast), and at riste is also in ristede løg (crispy fried onions).

sentence.da: En **brødrister** gør brødet varmt og sprødt.
sentence.en: A toaster makes the bread warm and crispy.

en brøk.explanation: "En brøk" means "a fraction", a part of a whole in math, like 1/2 or 3/4.

sentence.da: En fjerdedel af en pizza er en **brøk**.
sentence.en: A quarter of a pizza is a fraction.

en brønd.explanation: "En brønd" means "a well", a deep hole dug in the ground to reach water. A hole dug for oil is also a brønd: en oliebrønd (an oil well).

sentence.da: Vandet i landsbyen kommer op fra en dyb **brønd**.
sentence.en: The water in the village comes up from a deep well.

en buffet.explanation: "En buffet" means "a buffet", a long table with many dishes where you serve yourself. A hotel often has one for breakfast, usually for one fixed price.

sentence.da: Vi tager selv mad fra den store **buffet**.
sentence.en: We take food ourselves from the big buffet.

en bugt.explanation: "En bugt" means "a bay", a wide curve in the coast. It also means "a bend" in a river or road: en bugt i floden (a bend in the river).

sentence.da: En **bugt** er et sted, hvor havet går ind i landet.
sentence.en: A bay is a place where the sea goes into the land.

en bule.explanation: "En bule" means "a dent" in something hard, such as a car door, and also "a bump" on the body, for example on your forehead after a knock. In both cases, the surface is no longer smooth.

sentence.da: Der er en stor **bule** i bildøren efter ulykken.
sentence.en: There is a big dent in the car door after the accident.

en bums.explanation: "En bums" means "a pimple", a small red bump on the skin, for example on the face. A doctor would talk about akne (acne), the skin problem where you get many of them.

sentence.da: Jeg fik en **bums** på næsen, og den gjorde ondt.
sentence.en: I got a pimple on my nose, and it hurt.

en bund.explanation: "En bund" means "a bottom", the lowest part of something, such as a pan, a box or the sea. It is also the base of a pie: en tærtebund (a pie crust).

sentence.da: En kop har en flad **bund**.
sentence.en: A cup has a flat bottom.

en bundlinje.explanation: "En bundlinje" means "a bottom line", the last line in a company's accounts. It is also the usual word for a firm's final result: Bundlinjen er steget kraftigt (The bottom line has risen sharply).

sentence.da: Firmaets **bundlinje** viser, om det tjente penge i år.
sentence.en: The company's bottom line shows whether it made money this year.

en bunke.explanation: "En bunke" means "a pile", things lying on top of each other in no neat order: en bunke tøj (a pile of clothes). It also means "a large amount": en bunke penge (a large amount of money).

sentence.da: En **bunke** er rodet, men en stak er pæn.
sentence.en: A pile is messy, but a stack is neat.

en burger.explanation: "En burger" means "a burger", a patty of meat in a bun, usually with salad and sauce. A vegetarian one is en vegetarburger (a vegetarian burger).

sentence.da: En **burger** er kød mellem to stykker brød.
sentence.en: A burger is meat between two pieces of bread.

en bus.explanation: "En bus" means "a bus". To say you go by bus, use at tage bussen (to take the bus) or at køre med bus (to travel by bus).

sentence.da: En **bus** har plads til mange mennesker.
sentence.en: A bus has room for many people.
